Upgrade both ends together: each connector's own rating caps the total, however many wires reach it.

Pair it with Insulated or Shielded Wire. On plain Copper Wire it still moves only what that wire carries. Hold use on it with an empty hand, or look at it holding a wrench, to set how tight each wire hangs.
block.create_stats.advanced_topology_sca: The factory-wing grade: reaches further, and accounts for stress machine by machine.
Sits in a running shaft like the Field grade. Rotation passes straight through, and it reads the network from wherever it stands on the drivetrain.
Reaches 128 kinetic elements and adds per-machine stress, gearbox ratios and capacity accounting to the survey. Draws twice the Field grade's stress of its own, and the survey shows it doing so.

The clamp-on scanner at factory-wing reach, running on Forge Energy.

Craft it up from a Topology Scanner Probe. Point a Display Link at it to feed a Stats Display and unlock that panel's Topology tab.
block.create_stats.air_fryer.tooltip: A countertop convection fryer, wired for power rather than plugged in.
block.create_stats.air_fryer.tooltip.pla: Wire the terminal on the back, and leave the block in front of it clear for the drawer.
block.create_stats.air_fryer.tooltip.shi: Fast at food and deliberately slow at anything else. A hopper above feeds raw food in, a hopper below takes cooked food out, and a redstone pulse presses start. Opening the drawer or running out of power pauses the timer rather than losing the batch.
block.create_stats.air_fryer.tooltip.usa: Switch it on up top, pull the drawer out, fill the basket and press start. It dings when the batch is done.
block.create_stats.arc_furnace.tooltip: Alloys two charges under an electric arc. The heaviest load this mod has.
block.create_stats.arc_furnace.tooltip.p: Power goes into the conduit gland on the back, and only the back. The hatch and the console face you when placed.
block.create_stats.arc_furnace.tooltip.s: Tap I 128, II 512, III 1,152 FE/t; II half time, III a third. Lost arc: 1s restrike, no progress. Clean run bonus at Tap I; 25%+ stalled leaves slag.
block.create_stats.arc_furnace.tooltip.u: Right-click to open it: master switch, the three transformer taps, the pot and the buffer. Belts and funnels load the two charge slots and unload the product and the slag.
block.create_stats.auto_transmission_clu: Automatic stress governor for a kinetic shaft line
Place it inline between a power source and the branch you want to regulate
Auto-adjusts shaft speed to keep stress inside your chosen band.
Right-click to set the stress band and min/max RPM limits
block.create_stats.battle_screen_display: Display Link command bridge for Battle Observer feeds
Mount it on a sturdy wall face like a dedicated operator display
Shows only observer feeds received through Display Link refreshes.
Link Battle Observers into it with Create Display Links, then right-click to open the bridge
block.create_stats.biofuel_burner.toolti: Burns plant matter for Forge Energy. No shaft, no stress, no rotation.

Power leaves the back and the two flanks, never the front (that is the firebox door) and never the top (that is the fuel mouth). Feed it by hand, by hopper, by funnel or off a belt, and read how full the mouth is with a comparator.

Fixed 180 FE/t, half a Kinetic Dynamo, and the fuel decides the duration rather than the rate. Plant matter is priced by how much plant is in it: a log is worth the six planks a saw gets out of it, a hay bale is worth its nine wheat, a tuft of grass is worth a tuft of grass. The fire pauses while the buffer is full, so a burner nothing is drawing from does not eat its own hopper. The JEI Fuel page lists what burns for how long.

Anything bio goes in: any wood, leaves, saplings, flowers, crops, seeds, grass, wool, and anything a composter accepts, from this mod or any other. Coal and blaze rods do not, whatever their burn time. Nine loose items press into Compacted Biofuel on a Mechanical Press over a Basin, and what comes back out depends on what went in: nine tufts of grass make one brick, nine bamboo make two, nine carrots four, nine planks five. Logs are already dense and have no press recipe.
block.create_stats.solar_panel.tooltip: Polycrystalline wafers on a copper frame. No fuel, no shaft, no stress, and nothing at all at night.
block.create_stats.solar_panel.tooltip.p: Lay them flat with a clear view of the sky. Power leaves on any face but the top, which is the collector, and panels touching each other are one circuit: a single cable against a single panel feeds the whole roof. The frame rail disappears between joined panels, so a real roof looks like one field of cells and a scattered handful looks like a scattered handful.
block.create_stats.solar_panel.tooltip.s: Output follows the sun: a sine peaking at noon, so a whole day averages about a third of the peak figure. Rain is x0.35, a thunderstorm x0.15, night nothing. Sky light above the panel scales it, so glass passes almost everything, leaves pass some and a roof passes none. Panels joined into an array share a bonus of a quarter per factor of nine in count, capped at x1.5 at eighty one panels, a nine by nine roof. Each panel counts toward it by how much sky it catches, and a panel under another panel catches none.
block.create_stats.solar_panel.tooltip.u: The entry grade, at 0.6 of the Reinforced figure. Nine of these is a little over half a Kinetic Dynamo, for no rotation at all.
block.create_stats.reinforced_solar_pane: Monocrystalline cells under a steel frame. The grade every solar figure in this mod is quoted against.

block.create_stats.photovoltaic_array.to: Near-black cells behind tinted glass in an anodised frame. The most output per block, and the least per ingot.

1.6 times the Reinforced figure per block. Worth building where roof area is the thing you are short of rather than materials; where area is cheap, more of the plain grade is the better buy, because the array bonus counts panels and not output.
block.create_stats.blank_monitor_bezel.t: Empty screen frame. Decoration only, no block entity, does not accept Display Links.
Mount it on any sturdy wall face
A blank frame for set-dressing server rooms and monitor walls. If you point a Display Link at it, it will read "Not a Display Target": that is expected, this block has no data behind it.
Looking for a wall display that actually shows data? Use the E-Ink Data Panel instead
block.create_stats.blast_shutter.tooltip: The armoured shutter. Slower, heavier, and rated like the blast door it belongs beside.

Click a 1x2 opening to center, or a wall face for a flush 6px mount. Wrench cycles the 3 mounts, sneak-wrench sets a whole bank. Hold one, look at a column to grow it, up to 8 tall. Adjacent same-height columns link into one bank. Powers from any face: cable, Indoor Cable, or Appliance Cord.

No hand release, redstone I/O, or clearance, ever. Whole bank charges before moving, so an unpaid bank stays put, never half-seals. Taller = slower, costlier, bigger buffer. No power holds position; open, leaves stow fully clear.

3 triggers: lockdown seals every shutter, panel toggle seals one bank, dusk flag closes at night/opens dawn. Fire release forces every shutter open, beats both. Click with a shutter in hand: grows it a block taller.
block.create_stats.bread_slicer.tooltip: A counter-top slicer that cuts a loaf into slices.
block.create_stats.bulk_washer.tooltip: A front-loading washer that runs every splashing recipe in the game, one block instead of a fan tower.
block.create_stats.bulk_washer.tooltip.p: Power and water go into the back, and the underside takes water too. Items go in through the back or the inlet port on one flank, and washed items leave through the outlet port on the other flank or drop straight down into a hopper.
block.create_stats.bulk_washer.tooltip.s: Runs Create's washing recipes. Holds 256 items; only washed items reach the door/output. Eco cheap+slow, Full fast+pricey, Half between; water flat 20 mB/item. Losing power/water/off pauses without destroying the load.
block.create_stats.bulk_washer.tooltip.u: Press power, open the door and load it, shut the door, press start. Start is a latch, so a belt-fed washer is switched on once and left alone. The door will not open while the drum is turning: switch it off first.
block.create_stats.bus_duct.tooltip: The heavy indoor grade: low steel busway with a bolted joint every other block. Third of four.
block.create_stats.bus_duct.tooltip.plac: Lay it like any cable. Worth it between your generators and your distribution panel, where everything has to fit through.
block.create_stats.cable_diagnostic_junc: A splice with a meter in it: everything landing on the box becomes one circuit.
Mount it on any sturdy wall face, then run cable into the glands on the top and bottom

It joins runs regardless of dye colour, so it is how you tie two circuits together on purpose. The isolator cuts the splice dead without mining cable, and the card inside the door lists every fault code the screen can show.
Right-click the door to open it; pull the handle on the right flank to isolate the box.
block.create_stats.cable_tray.tooltip: A heavy industrial cable channel, sized for the run that feeds a room.
block.create_stats.caged_bulkhead_lamp.t: A caged industrial lamp for factory walls and ceilings.
Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click, and turns to face you. A wrench turns it another quarter.
Always needs cable power, and no config setting exempts it. A redstone signal switches it off rather than on. Sixteen dye colours are supported.
Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it.
block.create_stats.calculator.tooltip: Compact calculator block for quick math and graphing
block.create_stats.calculator.tooltip.pl: Place matching blocks side by side, or sneak-place to auto-fill a 2x3 panel
block.create_stats.calculator.tooltip.sh: Sneak while placing to auto-fill a 2x3 panel; Scientific mode adds x, ^, and functions.
block.create_stats.calculator.tooltip.us: Press the face buttons for quick math, or click the display to open the full screen
block.create_stats.capacitor_bank.toolti: Stores Forge Energy and shows the charge on its face.
Stack them. Touching banks pool into one battery, so a wall needs a single connector rather than one per block.
Merged banks hold more than the sum of their parts. Grids serve machines before storage, so a bank charges from surplus and discharges only to cover a real shortfall. Tunable in [power.storage].
A pool fills from the bottom up and drains from the top down: lit blocks are charge, dark blocks are headroom.
block.create_stats.coffee_machine.toolti: A lever espresso machine, plumbed for power rather than steam.
Wire the back for power and give the lever headroom.
Drop Cocoa Beans in the hopper, lock the portafilter, stand a mug on the tray and pull the lever.
block.create_stats.contactor.tooltip: A twin-coil contactor: redstone on its left makes the left pole, on its right the right pole, on both all three.
block.create_stats.contactor.tooltip.pla: Hang it on a wall, or lay it on a floor or ceiling top away from you. Wire a supply to a line stud on top and the load stud below it to what it feeds: each pole is its own circuit.
block.create_stats.contactor.tooltip.usa: A signal on its left side makes L1 to T1, on its right side L3 to T3, and both together make L2 to T2 as well. A wrench turns it normally closed, which inverts every pole; a right-click reads it. It gives no redstone; a comparator reads its busiest pole.
block.create_stats.contactor.tooltip.shi: Hold a wire near it to see its six studs. The middle bridge hangs from a bar between the two armatures, so one coil only tilts it half way. A pole that opens under load throws sparks sized by the current it breaks.
block.create_stats.control_clutch.toolti: Controller-driven clutch for a kinetic shaft line
Place it inline on the branch you want a controller to start or stop
Simple pass-through clutch with controller-facing state reporting and comparator signal output.
It has no UI; right-click it to check the linked controller and current signal
block.create_stats.damage_observer.toolt: Named Display Link source for Battle Bridge roles
Mount it on a sturdy face; the observer watches the space directly in front of it
Look at it to preview the watched block or area; use a Display Link to feed a Battle Bridge.
Right-click to name the zone, set its role, and choose Single Block, Local Area, or Behind Box
block.create_stats.data_dial.tooltip: Wall-mounted gauge for live machine and Display Link values
block.create_stats.data_dial.tooltip.pla: Mount it on a sturdy machine face or switch it to Linked mode
block.create_stats.data_dial.tooltip.shi: Sneak-right-click to switch between Local and Linked mode.
block.create_stats.data_dial.tooltip.usa: Right-click to cycle metric; comparator output follows the selected reading
block.create_stats.dispatch_board.toolti: Public operations board for a station's freight manifest
Right-click a Create station first to link this dispatch board
Right-click a Create station to link the board item before placing it; sneak-right-click a placed board with a linked clipboard to relink it later
Public live-ops board for one linked station; the clipboard still handles manifest authoring while the board focuses on status and order actions.
Right-click to view the live dispatch screen; operators can dismiss or reset delivery orders from the board
block.create_stats.dome_lamp.tooltip: A simple opal dome for interiors.
block.create_stats.dome_lamp.tooltip.pla: Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click.
block.create_stats.dome_lamp.tooltip.shi: Always needs cable power, and no config setting exempts it. A redstone signal switches it off rather than on. Sixteen dye colours are supported.
block.create_stats.dome_lamp.tooltip.usa: Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it.
block.create_stats.double_switch.tooltip: Two independent switches on one plate, for two circuits.
Place it against any face: it mounts flush on walls, floors and ceilings.
The left gang powers one side of the block and the right gang the other. Both drive the block behind.
block.create_stats.duplex_power_outlet.t: Two CEE 7/3 sockets in one plate that runs the full width of the block.
Mount it on the room face of a wall with cable behind it, then bore through
The same socket as the single, twice over and on one bore. The plate meets the block edges, so a row of them reads as one length of trunking rather than as separate plates.
Pilot lamp: grey for no supply, green for live, amber at the socket's limit
block.create_stats.eink_panel.tooltip: Electronic paper. Shows one number from a Display Link, and holds it with the power off.
block.create_stats.eink_panel.tooltip.pl: Mount it on any sturdy wall face; it needs no power and gives off no light
block.create_stats.eink_panel.tooltip.sh: A flat, unlit wall readout for corridors and control rooms. Reads plain Display Link text from any Create block, and every structured metric from this mod's own instruments.
block.create_stats.eink_panel.tooltip.us: Point a Display Link at it from any Create or Create Stats source, then right-click the panel to cycle through the metrics that source offers
block.create_stats.emergency_lamp.toolti: A maintained twin-spot with a charge pilot on its face.
Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click, and turns to face you. A wrench turns it another quarter.

block.create_stats.factory_logic_control: Branch computer that pauses linked clutch lines when watched rows go idle
Insert a machine card and a clutch link card in the same row to bind one watched branch
Best with Mechanical Press and Mechanical Mixer setups; other watched rows only use nearby belt, inventory, and dropped-item heuristics.
Right-click to open the logic screen; it starts with 3 rows and expands as you fill more
block.create_stats.fe_battery_controller: Manages every capacitor bank wired to it as one pooled reserve.
Six built-in terminals, no Power Connector needed. Three cool studs are inputs A, B and C; three copper studs are outputs 1, 2 and 3, one circuit each.

Each output holds a charge floor the reserve won't cross; drag its gauge tick to set it, so the base sheds bottom-up, not all at once. Low reserve holds back generation to refill. Tunable in [power.batteryController].
Give every bank stack its own input instead of wiring banks to each other: nothing is in series, no connector is a single point of failure, and the reserve becomes one number.
block.create_stats.fe_motor.tooltip: Spends Forge Energy to turn its shaft: dial up to %s RPM and up to %s SU.
block.create_stats.filament_bulb.tooltip: A bare filament on a rose. The cheapest light in the set.
Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click.
Always needs cable power, and no config setting exempts it. A redstone signal switches it off rather than on. Sixteen dye colours are supported.
Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it.
block.create_stats.fire_sensor.tooltip: Watches for fire, lava and anything burning. Never switches off.
block.create_stats.fire_sensor.tooltip.p: Mounts on any wall, floor or ceiling and takes power on any face, so a cable beside it or an Indoor Cable bored through the surface behind it both feed it. It needs no wire terminal of its own.
block.create_stats.fire_sensor.tooltip.s: Releases every door for anyone, beating lockdown: fire outranks burglary. Entrance stays owner-only, so outside fire isn't a way in. Lapses 10s after. Needs a Home Security Panel on-circuit, no redstone I/O; unpowered = fault, red banner.
block.create_stats.fire_sensor.tooltip.u: Trips on fire, lava, a lit campfire or a burning creature within range. A hazard sensor ignores the house mode entirely and is watching in HOME, AWAY and CUSTOM alike, because a smoke alarm that can be switched off is a broken smoke alarm.
block.create_stats.flight_control_comput: On-contraption autopilot: pairs propellers with RPM Governors and runs the flight control loops
Place on a Sable contraption with a linked Gimbal Sensor; auto-discovers Altitude/Velocity sensors and Nav Tables on the same sub-level
Arm from the GUI to route your cockpit controls; linked Gimbal, Altitude, and Velocity sensors gate readiness. External RPM input forces STANDBY.
Right-click to open the GUI; bind propellers, governors, and burner redstone links there
block.create_stats.flood_lamp.tooltip: A yoke-mounted floodlight for yards, bays and anything outdoors.
block.create_stats.flood_lamp.tooltip.pl: Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click, and turns to face you. A wrench turns it another quarter.
block.create_stats.flood_lamp.tooltip.sh: Always needs cable power, and no config setting exempts it. A redstone signal switches it off rather than on. Sixteen dye colours are supported.
block.create_stats.flood_lamp.tooltip.us: Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it.
block.create_stats.flow_meter.tooltip: Fluid pipe that measures the throughput passing through it.
block.create_stats.flow_meter.tooltip.pl: Splice it into a fluid line; it auto-aligns with the adjacent pipe or fluid handler
block.create_stats.flow_meter.tooltip.sh: Moves fluid exactly like a copper pipe and can be waterlogged. Reports the fluid, its direction, the rate in mB per tick and the total volume moved, and can emit redstone when flow crosses a threshold set from a linked Stats Display.
block.create_stats.flow_meter.tooltip.us: Link it to a Stats Display with a Display Link to read its flow
block.create_stats.fluid_pump.tooltip: Pushes fluid down its pipe run for Forge Energy, up to %s mB/t.
block.create_stats.freight_manifest_clip: Station-linked manifest desk; its page shows live order progress
Right-click a Create station first to link this clipboard
Link it to a Create station first, then place it standing or wall-mounted
Right-click a linked desk to write the station's freight manifest. Once written, the page fills itself in: one bar per open order, and a red stamp when the whole board is done.
Right-click to write the manifest. Ctrl+S applies it, arrow keys move between lines, shift-click an item to add another line.
block.create_stats.garage_door_header.to: The drum the curtain winds into, and the run that measures the door.
Lay a run along the opening's top, as wide as the bay. Curtain hangs down as far as there's room, no rails, nothing to align. Hold one, look at a header to ghost-preview the next, same facing.

Capped at 12 deep, needs a wider drum past that. Auto-shortens over an obstruction, floors out clear. Governed like any door: clearance, lockdown, fire release, can be the entrance. Opens for cleared players/vehicles, reverses on someone closing on it.
Up to twelve blocks wide and twelve deep. Right click any hood or the curtain to work it, or wire it to redstone. Takes power on any face of any hood, or through a wall by boring a cable into one.
block.create_stats.high_bay_lamp.tooltip: A deep-shaded ceiling lamp for large open floors.
Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click.

Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it.
block.create_stats.holographic_projector: A flush emitter rail that projects live factory data above it
Place it on a solid block in a dashboard area or enable its nearby scanner
Right-click opens size, theme, projection, redstone and channel settings.
Right-click to open its settings, or sneak-right-click to cycle the display style
A field emitter that stands a measurement volume in the air above itself
Set it on a solid block with clear space overhead; the projection rises from between its four posts
Five render treatments, two layouts, and a volume you size in blocks. Channels are stacked in depth, so walking around it changes what is in front.
Right-click to open the console, or sneak-right-click to step the render style
block.create_stats.home_security_panel.t: A wall keypad that finds the security devices on its own circuit and decides who may use them.
Mounts flush on any wall and takes power on any face, so a cable beside it or an Indoor Cable bored through the wall behind it both feed it. It needs no wire terminal of its own.

Role = what you change; clearance = what you open, kept separate so a keyholder can't edit the roster. Access view grids person x device. Power only buys auto-search, never authority. Unpowered: dark, controls still work.
block.create_stats.security_relay.toolti: Turns one thing your security household decides, like a fire, a lockdown or a refused door, into a plain redstone signal: 0 or 15.
Stands on a floor with its faceplate toward you. The signal leaves through the back, at the red post, like an Observer's. Takes power on any face.

Right click the faceplate to choose what it watches and how it answers: Follow, Pulse or Hold. A house with a password asks for its code first. Press the red button to reset a held incident. If it says it is waiting, accept it here or at the Home Security Panel.
No power, no signal: wire supervision normally energised and invert it with a torch. It only reads the house; its signal opens no door and clears no lockdown.
relay.create_stats.condition.lockdown.bl: The household's lockdown, raised by an armed trip or tamper. Stays until the owner clears it.
relay.create_stats.condition.tamper.blur: An armed tamper the house accepted: a Tamper Sensor, three bad codes, a locker being mined.
relay.create_stats.condition.fire.blurb: Fire seen by the house's Fire Sensors. Clears only after a whole clean sweep.
relay.create_stats.condition.water.blurb: Water seen by the house's Water Sensors, kept separate from fire.
relay.create_stats.condition.denied.blur: A governed door, garage or locker turned somebody away.
relay.create_stats.condition.breached.bl: A door, garage or shutter reports its own structure breached.
relay.create_stats.condition.trouble.blu: An expected device is missing, out of reach, blind, silent or breached. Not knowing counts as trouble.
relay.create_stats.condition.mode.blurb: The house is in the mode you choose.
relay.create_stats.condition.healthy.blu: Everything it watches is available, it can reach the house and it has power. Wire it normally energised.

This relay's condition is not supported by this version.

Still happening. It can be reset once it is over.
message.create_stats.security_relay.conf: Only an owner or admin may change this relay.
Changed from another screen just now. This is the current setting; try again.
That condition is not supported by this version.
That condition cannot be used that way.
That device cannot be watched for this condition.

message.create_stats.security_relay.reti: Only an owner or admin may retire this relay.
It is holding an incident. Only the owner may decommission it now.
message.create_stats.security_relay.not_: The house asks for its code again. Use the relay to enter it.
Only an owner or admin of this house may accept the relay.
block.create_stats.home_security_panel.t: Right click to open it. Whoever places it becomes the owner, and the owner passes every device regardless of level. Give each device a required clearance from 1 to 5, give each player a clearance of their own, and a player passes when theirs meets the device's.
block.create_stats.indoor_cable.tooltip: A slim one-pixel cord that runs through the middle of its block instead of along a face.
Clips to the face you click and follows it. Right-click with an empty hand to move it to another surface, or to the middle of the block.
Sized for lamps, coolers and speakers rather than machines. Its limit is per run, so a spur off a trunk never throttles the trunk.
It powers everything it touches, and everything a bore takes it through. Dye it to split one circuit from another.
block.create_stats.induction_heater.gogg: No Induction Coil, stuck on passive Warm
block.create_stats.induction_heater.tool: Kinetic stove plate: heats Basins and Boilers with rotation instead of Blaze fuel.
Place it under a Basin or Boiler tank with a shaft feeding its underside
32 SU/RPM: 2,048 Warm, 4,096 Kindled, 8,192 Superheated, 16s per floor. Coil fuels the top two, wears with use. 30s campfire: 30/15/9s per tier, nothing flung on the floor.
64 RPM keeps it Warm. An Induction Coil unlocks Kindled at 128 RPM and Superheated at 256. Right-click with raw food to cook a whole stack on the plate.
block.create_stats.induction_range.toolt: An electric hob. Forge Energy in, heat out, at the setting you choose.
Wire it with Surface Cable or a Power Connector. The control panel faces you when placed.

Medium is Create Heated and High is Superheated, matching a fuelled Blaze Burner and a blaze cake exactly. A range also powers every range within one block, so a 3x3 bank runs off a single cable landing anywhere on its edge.
Right-click to turn the dial: off, Low 16 FE/t, Medium 64 FE/t, High 256 FE/t. Low cooks like a campfire, Medium also smelts, High also blasts.
block.create_stats.induction_smelter.too: Smelts and blasts at belt volume. Touching Smelters pool into one machine.
Power goes into the conduit gland on the back, and only the back. The mouth, the dial and the damper face you when placed. A whole bank needs one connection, anywhere on it.

15% faster, no fuel. 64 FE/t working, 12 FE/t idle. Cold start: 38,400 FE before the first item; under 2:40 idle, holding's cheaper, past it, cool down. Rate follows temperature; blasting needs 80%+ heat.

Right-click to open it: the muffle itself, the damper, the buffer and the temperature. Click the lever on the front to set the damper without opening anything. Belts and funnels work the whole bank through any module.
block.create_stats.industrial_alternator: Converts shaft rotation into Forge Energy. The dense grade.
Drive the shaft on its bottom face; energy leaves every other face.
Build this when floor space is the thing you are short of. It is not the efficient one; it is the one that fits.
The most output from a single block, and more stress than power.
block.create_stats.industrial_power_conn: The trunk grade wire terminal, matched to the HV Line.
Mount it like the other connectors: on a generator, battery, or powered machine.
Holds six wires rather than four, so one feed can fan out to five legs.
Its rate is the sum of its wires, so one HV Line fills it, or two Shielded Wires. Hold use on it with an empty hand, or look at it holding a wrench, to set how tight each wire hangs.
block.create_stats.industrial_topology_s: The survey grade: a whole base at once, with load history and bottleneck ranking.
Sits in a running shaft like the lower grades. It reads the network from wherever it stands.

Reaches 512 kinetic elements and adds a two-minute load trend, a heaviest-consumer ranking and an overstress projection. Draws four times the Field grade's stress of its own; the survey shows that draw like any other machine's.
Craft it up from an Advanced Topology Scanner. Point a Display Link at it to feed a Stats Display and unlock that panel's Topology tab.
The survey-grade clamp-on scanner: a whole base, on Forge Energy.
Clamp it to a kinetic block's face and give it a solid FE supply. The readout faces you.
Reaches 512 elements with load history, bottleneck ranking and an overstress projection, drawing FE instead of stress. Without power it will not scan, and it says so.
Craft it up from an Advanced Topology Scanner Probe. Point a Display Link at it to feed a Stats Display and unlock that panel's Topology tab.
block.create_stats.isolator_switch.toolt: A chunky lockable rotary for the wall beside a machine.
Place it against any face: it mounts flush on walls, floors and ceilings.
Emits a redstone signal, strongly into the block behind it. The handle turns a quarter turn when thrown.
block.create_stats.kinetic_dynamo.toolti: Converts shaft rotation into Forge Energy. The middle grade.
Drive the shaft on its bottom face; energy leaves every other face.
The grade every other figure is quoted against, and it runs whatever the power settings say. Tunable in [power.generator]; the other two grades scale off it.
Matches a Crafts and Additions alternator exactly, on output and on stress. Attach a Power Connector or run cable to move the energy.
block.create_stats.kinetic_flywheel.gogg: Bank of %s sharing the load · %s SU total, %s%% average
Waiting for surplus, the network has none spare
Coasting on friction, ~%s of reserve left
Out of circuit: not charging, not sourcing, keeping its reserve
Holding §f%s§r RPM (Auto, the line's own speed)
Holding §f%s§r RPM, slowed from %s to carry the load
Standing by, the line has nothing spare
Needs §f%s%%§r before it will carry the line again
Runs §f%s§r at this load (%s%% of rated)
Add a Flywheel to raise the stage
block.create_stats.kinetic_flywheel.tool: Kinetic inertia bank: stores surplus network power and gives it back to cover a gap.
Branch a shaft into its single end connection to spin the wheel up

It charges only from spare capacity, so it cannot overstress the line it is buffering, and becomes a source when nothing else is driving the line or when something is and cannot carry the load. Either way it holds one speed, so machines see steady RPM and the reserve only decides how long.
Right-click with a Create Flywheel to add a mass stage; sneak-right-click with an empty hand to pop one back. A redstone signal takes it out of circuit
block.create_stats.klaxon_alarm.tooltip: Hardwired alarm annunciator with a struck bell and a needle dial.
Run a cable to it, and keep the block above clear for its head
Watches the whole FE circuit it is wired into, battery bank charge included, and rings when a rule trips.
Right-click the panel to set rules; press ACK to silence, RESET to clear
block.create_stats.load_balancer.tooltip: Splits one driven shaft into two governed output branches
The face marked with two blue bars is the input; left and right are outputs, and merged branches are invalid
The blue marked shaft is the input; left and right shafts are outputs. Scroll the front dial with a wrench to set the split, or right-click to open the full controls.
Scroll the front dial to set the split; right-click for the stress band and Strict or Elastic sharing
block.create_stats.main_breaker.tooltip: A rotary disconnect. The handle sits over centre until you push it past, then the spring throws it the rest of the way.
Place it against any face: it mounts flush on walls, ceilings and floors, and the handle reads the same on all of them.

METERED (default): passes the lesser terminal span, names the limiter. Inverse-time trip: 2x = set time, 3x = a third, 8x = instant. PASSTHROUGH fuses both terminals, unrated/untripped, to the next breaker/panel/box. Handle cuts power either way.

Right-click throws it: across = open (O), up = closed (I). Supply to amber INPUT, protected run to cyan OUTPUT; opening cuts downstream entirely. Trip hangs it halfway, throw twice to reset+close. Paddle by the lamp picks METERED/PASSTHROUGH. Sneak+empty hand padlocks it.
block.create_stats.creative_main_breaker: The Main Breaker in creative dress. Same mechanism, same throw, and it cannot be broken.
Place it against any face, the same as the ordinary one.

Right-click to throw it. Closed, it supplies BOTH terminals with as much as their wire will carry; open, both are dead. It makes its own power, so it has no supply side and both terminals are outlets. It never trips.
item.create_stats.blueberry.tooltip: A handful of blueberries, picked from the bush.
item.create_stats.blueberry.tooltip.usag: Plant one on grass or dirt to start a bush. Right-click a ripe bush to pick it without breaking it, and it will fruit again in half the time it first took.
item.create_stats.cake_mold.tooltip: A fluted tin. The Oven gives it back with the cake.
item.create_stats.cake_mold.tooltip.usag: Hold it under a Spout and fill it with flavoured Cake Batter, then feed the filled tin to an Oven. One tin does the job over and over; nothing in the pipeline consumes it.
item.create_stats.carrot_cake_mold.toolt: A tin of carrot batter, waiting on an Oven.
item.create_stats.cinnamon.tooltip: Quills of bark cut from a cinnamon shrub.
item.create_stats.cinnamon.tooltip.usage: Plant a quill on grass or dirt to grow a new shrub. Not food on its own; it is a flavour for the Basin, and eating raw bark is not a meal.
item.create_stats.cinnamon_cake_mold.too: A tin of cinnamon batter, waiting on an Oven.
item.create_stats.blueberry_cake_mold.to: A tin of blueberry batter, waiting on an Oven.
item.create_stats.cacao_cake_mold.toolti: A tin of cacao batter, waiting on an Oven.
item.create_stats.flour.tooltip: Retired. Craft it into Wheat Flour.
item.create_stats.flour.tooltip.usage: No longer used. Cake batter takes Create's Wheat Flour now; craft this into it, one for one.
item.create_stats.strawberry.tooltip: Sweet, and better farmed than foraged.
item.create_stats.strawberry.tooltip.usa: Plants on farmland, and also on plain dirt or grass, which is how wild ones grow. Farmland is still worth it: moist soil grows them noticeably faster.
item.create_stats.vanilla_bean.tooltip: A cured pod off a jungle vine.
item.create_stats.vanilla_bean.tooltip.u: Plant it on the side of a jungle log, the way cocoa grows. It will not take on any other wood, and it will not grow on the ground at all.
item.create_stats.vanilla_cake_mold.tool: A tin of vanilla batter, waiting on an Oven.
item.create_stats.strawberry_cake_mold.t: A tin of strawberry batter, waiting on an Oven.
message.create_stats.main_breaker.no_stu: Aim at one of the two studs on the deck
message.create_stats.main_breaker.locked: Padlocked. The handle and its wiring are held where they are.
message.create_stats.main_breaker.padloc: Padlocked: take the lock off before throwing it
Padlocked: take the lock off before rewiring it
message.create_stats.main_breaker.reset: Trip cleared. Throw it again to close.
message.create_stats.main_breaker.mode_m: METERED: two circuits, rated by the thinner terminal, measured, and it trips
message.create_stats.main_breaker.mode_p: PASSTHROUGH: one circuit straight through, nothing rated, metered or tripped
block.create_stats.mini_display.tooltip: Compact wall-mounted readout for item, fluid, boiler, and kinetic stats
Mount it on a sturdy face, or place two side by side for a 2x1 display
Compact wall-mounted stats readout; link it or pair two side by side for a wider display.
Right-click to configure local or linked readouts; hold a filter item to pin storage lines
block.create_stats.motion_sensor.tooltip: Watches for people without clearance, and for anything hostile.
Mounts on any wall, floor or ceiling and takes power on any face, so a cable beside it or an Indoor Cable bored through the surface behind it both feed it. It needs no wire terminal of its own.
Armed trip seals every door, even the owner. Entrance is the one way back in, owner-only until cleared. Needs a Home Security Panel on-circuit, no redstone I/O; unpowered = fault, red banner.

Trips on players below required clearance, and hostile mobs. Cleared players pass freely. Ignores animals, villagers, golems, armour stands. Follows panel mode: HOME logs, AWAY arms, CUSTOM own switch.
block.create_stats.open_frame_dynamo.too: Converts shaft rotation into Forge Energy. The frugal grade.
Drive the shaft on its bottom face; energy leaves every other face.
Build this when rotation is the thing you are short of: two of them out-produce one Kinetic Dynamo on the stress one Kinetic Dynamo spends.
The least output of the three and much the best value per stress unit.
block.create_stats.overflow_gate.tooltip: Belt-side splitter that routes filtered outputs first and overflow last
Place it on a horizontal cased belt like a Create tunnel
Prioritizes filtered and open outputs first, then sends leftovers to the chosen overflow side.
Use side filters and the top selector to define Any and Overflow routing
block.create_stats.pa_brain.tooltip: The brain of a public address system: it watches, decides what is worth saying, and says it.
block.create_stats.pa_brain.tooltip.plac: Wire the terminal on its back for power, then open it and pick what it should watch.
block.create_stats.pa_brain.tooltip.shif: Listening is cheap, looking costs more, and talking is charged by the word.
block.create_stats.pa_brain.tooltip.usag: It reads the panels, alarm devices and machines in range and announces what changes.
block.create_stats.panel_lamp.tooltip: A flush recessed panel, barely proud of the surface.
block.create_stats.panel_lamp.tooltip.pl: Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click.
block.create_stats.panel_lamp.tooltip.sh: Always needs cable power, and no config setting exempts it. A redstone signal switches it off rather than on. Sixteen dye colours are supported.
block.create_stats.panel_lamp.tooltip.us: Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it.
block.create_stats.path_scanner.tooltip: Loaded-chunk drivability scanner for Pathfinder Computer routes
Face it along the intended driving direction; it scans forward and side chunks without force-loading them
Small lens and cap lamps show scan activity, cached coverage, and unknown chunk coverage.
Send its summary to a Pathfinder Computer through Display Link; use the GUI to tune range and unknown policy
block.create_stats.pathfinder_computer.t: Route computer for scanner-guided Otomobil and craft Auto guidance
Receive a Path Scanner through Display Link, then forward guidance to a Flight Control Computer
Small lamps show Scanner input, FCC output, thinking, accepted route, retained route, and rejected route states.
Plans a retained local route from loaded scanner data and exposes route, hold, and link state in its GUI
block.create_stats.pendant_lamp.tooltip: An enamel cone on a flex, hung from a brass ceiling rose.
Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click.
Always needs cable power, and no config setting exempts it. A redstone signal switches it off rather than on. Sixteen dye colours are supported.
Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it.
block.create_stats.power_connector.toolt: A wire terminal that moves Forge Energy point to point.
Mount it on a generator, battery, or powered machine.

Nothing passes through a connector faster than its own grade, hub or not. What it hands its block is the sum of the wires and cable meeting it, up to that grade. Range, rate and buffer are tunable in [power.wiring].

Span Copper Wire between two connectors. It pulls from a source behind it and feeds a machine behind it. Hold use on it with an empty hand, or look at it holding a wrench, to set how tight each wire hangs.
block.create_stats.pdu_cabinet.tooltip: The PDU controller in a two-block instrument cabinet.
block.create_stats.pdu_cabinet.tooltip.p: Eight rear studs, numbered from top to bottom, plus a rear BUS cable boss. Feed FE through either lower side boss. Requires two blocks of space and a solid floor.
block.create_stats.pdu_cabinet.tooltip.u: Right-click the front to open the door, even with an item held. Click the door or frame to close it. Click the revealed screen for PDU controls. Instruments show actual delivered FE/t; the slim input columns show utilization.
block.create_stats.pdu_cabinet.tooltip.s: Nine pilot lamps, one per output plus the BUS: green carrying, dim green idle, amber held back, red flashing tripped, cyan feeding in, dark open or unwired. Rear studs keep the original PDU output numbers, ratings, priorities and breakers. The BUS is the ninth output.
block.create_stats.power_distribution_un: Serves its branch by priority and sheds what it cannot power.
Nine legs, each with its own breaker: eight studs on the top bus bar plus the cable boss at the back. Feed FE in through either side boss.
A shed device coasts on its own reserve and reads amber LOAD SHED, not red NO POWER. Right-click a row to lock a machine on so it is never shed, or off so it never runs. Tunable in [power.pdu].
Three modes. Off shares evenly. Manual serves Critical first and sheds down the tiers. Auto measures what your generators actually make and runs the largest set that supply sustains.
block.create_stats.portable_power_interf: Charges a train's Capacitor Banks at a station, or draws power back out of them.
Put one on the train facing out and one at the station facing the track, up to two blocks apart. Wire the station one like any machine; the train one needs nothing.

On a side face, hold right-click on the box showing a rate to pick a direction and a speed: the green top row charges the train, the amber bottom row draws from it. The box showing a percentage is the charge it always leaves behind: the station's while charging, the train's while drawing. Redstone switches it off. A comparator reads the docked train's charge, 1 to 15.

Charge lives in the Capacitor Banks the train carries, and in Crafts & Additions accumulators if that mod is present. A train waits as long as its schedule says; the Train charge condition waits for a percentage. Other contraptions stay until full, empty or held by the floor.
block.create_stats.power_track.tooltip: Train track with a centre conductor rail that charges trains, or collects from them.
block.create_stats.power_track.tooltip.s: Stations assemble along one kind of track: make a platform all Power Track, or none.
block.create_stats.power_track.tooltip.p: Lay it like any train track; it joins ordinary track. The conductor rail stops in a ramp at junctions, at Section Insulators and where ordinary track begins, and for a block and a half either side of a change of grade; a curve that climbs has none.
block.create_stats.power_track.tooltip.u: Put a Track Feeder beside it to tie a section to a circuit, and fit Current Collectors under the cars.
block.create_stats.power_track.tooltip.s: A section is the rail between Section Insulators. Junctions and changes of grade gap the rail, not the section: jumper cables carry it on, but a train standing in a gap does not charge. Goggles name every gap. A car in unloaded chunks exchanges nothing.
block.create_stats.track_feeder.tooltip: Ties one section of Power Track to an FE circuit, to supply trains or collect from them.
Click the Power Track where its cable should land, then place the cabinet beside the line. Wire its back like any machine.
On the door, hold right-click on the window showing a rate to pick Supply, Collect or Auto and a rate; the window showing a percentage sets the floor. Redstone switches it off.

Supply never drains the station's banks below the floor; Collect leaves every train that much charge; Auto supplies above it and collects below it. The needle swings right while supplying and left while collecting; the lantern shows the rail as a Section Insulator's lamps do: green energised, amber collecting, dark idle.
block.create_stats.section_insulator.too: Ends a section of conductor rail: nothing crosses its gap. One lamp for each side shows that side's section.
Click the Power Track where the gap should be, then place the board beside the line. It turns itself parallel to the track.
Green: a feeder energises that side. Amber: a feeder collects from it. Dark: dead rail. A train standing across the gap exchanges with one side only.
block.create_stats.current_collector.too: Shoe gear for a train car: rides the centre conductor rail and moves FE between it and the car's Capacitor Banks.
%s a shoe, %s shoes a car count (%s)
Hang it under a car one block above the track, on the car's centre line or a block to either side: its shoe slides across to the rail. 2 to 3 blocks from a bogie it follows curves best.

On a live section the car charges; on a collecting one it gives, down to that feeder's floor. The gear turns to lie along the car whichever way it was placed. Goggles say what the shoe meets: the rail, a gap, or why it cannot reach.
create_stats.jei.power_track.info:
Create's train track with a centre conductor rail on porcelain chairs. A Track Feeder beside the line ties the rail to an FE circuit; a Current Collector under a car rides it and moves FE between the rail and the Capacitor Banks the car carries.

A section is the conductor rail between two Section Insulators. A junction does not end one: the rail stops in a ramp clear of the points and jumper cables carry the section across. A change of grade does the same, a block and a half either side of a slope's foot or crest and along the whole of a curve that climbs, because a bogie pitching over the kink would strike a rail there. A train standing in any of these gaps does not charge, and the track's goggles name each one. One section carries %s, one shoe %s, and a car counts two shoes, %s.

A station assembles a train along one kind of track only, so lay a whole platform in Power Track or none of it. A car in unloaded chunks exchanges nothing.
create_stats.jei.track_feeder.info:
Ties one section of Power Track to an FE circuit, the way a Portable Power Interface ties a docked train to one. Click the track where its cable should land, then place the cabinet beside the line, and wire its back like any machine.

Supply puts the circuit's power on the rail for every car on the section, never draining the station's Capacitor Banks below the floor. Collect takes power from passing cars, leaving each the floor's charge. Auto supplies while the station has charge above the floor and collects while it is short, so a train running between two Auto feeders carries power from the station that has it to the one that needs it. Two feeders on different circuits also share a section's rail between them; two on one circuit never do.

The rate runs from %s to %s. The needle swings right while supplying and left while collecting, by what is moving; the lantern shows the rail's state in the Section Insulator's language, green while this feeder energises it, amber while it collects from it, dark while idle, and lights the ground beside the cubicle at night. On a Power Distribution Unit the feeder is a Low priority load. Redstone switches it off.
create_stats.jei.section_insulator.info:
Ends a section of Power Track. Click the track where the gap should be, then place the board beside the line; it turns itself parallel to the track. The conductor rail stops either side in a white insulated end and nothing crosses.

Each lamp shows the section on its own side: green while a feeder energises it, amber while one collects from it, dark while it is dead. A car standing across the gap exchanges with one side only, and a train never charges on one section while giving on another in the same tick.
create_stats.jei.current_collector.info:
Shoe gear for a train car. Hang it under a car one block above the track, on the car's centre line or a block to either side, two or three blocks from a bogie; its sled slides the shoe across to the centre conductor rail, the shoe trails away from the nearest bogie, and the gear turns to lie along the car however it was placed.

On a live section the car's Capacitor Banks charge; on a collecting one they give, down to the collecting feeder's floor. Each shoe carries %s and a car counts %s shoes. In a gap the shoe drops to its stop and touches nothing; landing on live rail under load it arcs.
block.create_stats.power_limiter.mode.al: Redstone is ignored. The limit always applies.
block.create_stats.power_limiter.mode.an: The limit scales with signal strength: full at 15, shut at 0.
block.create_stats.power_limiter.mode.si: Shut until powered, then the limit applies.
The limit applies until a signal arrives, then the gate shuts.
block.create_stats.power_limiter.state.l: Limiting: the cap is holding power back
block.create_stats.power_limiter.state.n: Nothing on the gland end to feed
Nothing wired to the brass terminal
block.create_stats.power_limiter.state.s: Shut: nothing is being let through
block.create_stats.power_limiter.tooltip: Inline throttle, wired into a circuit between a supply and a load.
Supply into the brass terminal, load off the cable gland at the far end. Either takes cable, a connector and wire, or a machine bolted straight on.
Not a grid member: the boundary between its two circuits, which is what enforces the cap. Each direction capped separately. A loop on both terminals is refused as a fault.

Right-click for the slider, the redstone modes and a live trace. A wrench on the cam opens the value board; a wrench anywhere else turns the block. Sneak right-click clears the total. A comparator gives the load against the cap, 1 to 15.
block.create_stats.power_meter.fault.no_: Nothing on the gland end to feed
Nothing wired to the brass terminal
block.create_stats.power_meter.goggle.ba: Backed up: the load is not taking it
block.create_stats.power_meter.tooltip: Inline submeter, wired into a circuit between a supply and a load.
block.create_stats.power_meter.tooltip.p: Supply into the brass terminal, load off the cable gland at the far end. Either takes cable, a connector and wire, or a machine bolted straight on.
block.create_stats.power_meter.tooltip.s: The meter is not part of the grid: it is the boundary between the circuit feeding it and the circuit it feeds, which is what makes the figure a real measurement rather than a share of a pool. One circuit reaching both terminals is refused and reported as a fault.
block.create_stats.power_meter.tooltip.u: Right-click for the reading and its history; sneak right-click resets the peak and total. A comparator gives the load against the peak, 1 to 15.
block.create_stats.power_outlet.tooltip: A CEE 7/3 wall socket: the room-side end of a circuit that runs inside the wall.
Mount it on the room face of a wall with cable behind it, then bore through

Point a Cable Bore at the socket and click: the sleeve is cut through the wall and the circuit behind it feeds the plate. Anything standing beside the socket then draws from it, up to 512 FE/t, with no wire between them.
Pilot lamp: grey for no supply, green for live, amber at the socket's limit
block.create_stats.powered_door.tooltip: A two-tall door that runs on FE and answers to a Home Security Panel.
Takes power on any face of either of its two blocks, and a Cable Bore will drive a sleeve through a jamb or a lintel straight into it, so the run can stay inside the wall. Two placed side by side become a double door when their hinges face outward, and then they move as one leaf in two halves.

Keeps its own roster, so it refuses even if the panel's unpowered, unloaded, or smashed. No power = no motor; hand-shifting the leaf depends on the panel's fail-secure setting. Wrench cycles opening, sneak+wrench flips hinge, sneak+empty hand toggles a pair's interlock.

Right click to work it, or drive it from redstone. A Home Security Panel on the same circuit finds it on its own, gives it a required clearance, and opens it for anybody who clears that level as they walk up to it. Until a panel claims it, it opens for anyone.
block.create_stats.production_detector.t: A window into a chest, vault, tank, belt or battery: what it holds, what is moving, and when it fills or runs dry
Place it with its back against a chest, vault, tank, belt or battery to read it, or aim a Display Link at its screen to read a block anywhere in the link's reach

Counts every item coming in and going out, a minute at a time, and keeps three days of history on its chart paper. Its lamps light at LOW, FULL and STALL; its two side outputs and its comparator follow the LOW and HIGH marks.
Right-click for the contents, watched items and the books. Put an item in the sample cup to watch it; turn the side dials to set LOW and HIGH. Press TEST to acknowledge an alarm or test the lamps.
block.create_stats.push_button.tooltip: A push-button plate that latches: press for on, press again for off.
block.create_stats.push_button.tooltip.p: Place it against any face: it mounts flush on walls, floors and ceilings.
block.create_stats.push_button.tooltip.u: Latches like a real push-button light switch: press for on, press again for off.
block.create_stats.rocker_switch.tooltip: An ordinary wall light switch. Stays where you put it.
Place it against any face: it mounts flush on walls, floors and ceilings.
Breaks the cable run it sits in: open the switch and everything downstream goes dark. Also emits redstone.
block.create_stats.rotary_dimmer_dial.to: A panel-instrument rotary dimmer: a fluted knob beside a ten segment bargraph.
Place it against any face: it mounts flush on walls, floors and ceilings.

Aim at it and scroll to turn it, one notch per 10%, with an empty hand or a wrench. Right-click pushes it on or off; sneak-right-click steps it down. Bind lamps to it with a Switch Link Card and they follow its level. Like any switch it also breaks the cable run it sits in, and emits redstone while on.
block.create_stats.rotary_dimmer_puck.to: A flush rotary dimmer: a floating puck with a light pipe ring that fills as you turn.
Place it against any face: it mounts flush on walls, floors and ceilings.

Aim at it and scroll to turn it, one notch per 10%, with an empty hand or a wrench. Right-click pushes it on or off; sneak-right-click steps it down. Bind lamps to it with a Switch Link Card and they follow its level. Like any switch it also breaks the cable run it sits in, and emits redstone while on.
block.create_stats.time_switch.tooltip: A segment time switch: a 24 hour dial that turns with the day, and a slider at its rim for every hour.
block.create_stats.time_switch.tooltip.p: Place it against any face: it mounts flush on walls, floors and ceilings.
block.create_stats.time_switch.tooltip.u: Right-click a slider to push it in, which closes the circuit for that hour, or to draw it back out; hold and drag round the rim to set a run of hours. The slide on the right holds it on (I), off (0) or lets it follow the sliders (the clock). Hold the hub for Dusk to dawn, Daytime, Clear or Invert, or look at it with a wrench and scroll. Like any switch it breaks the cable run it sits in, gates fixtures bound to it with a Switch Link Card, and emits redstone while closed.
block.create_stats.rpm_governor.tooltip: Flight Control Computer actuator: asserts an exact signed RPM on its kinetic island
Place inline on the shaft driving a propeller; the FCC must own one Governor per propeller
Acts as a kinetic source, clamped to ±256 RPM. Idle on world load until the FCC reclaims it.
Bind via the Flight Control Computer GUI; releases automatically if the FCC stops responding
block.create_stats.safety_clutch.tooltip: Self-monitoring clutch that trips before a line overstresses
Place it inline on a shaft branch so it can watch that network
Trips on overload to cut power and protect the line.
Right-click to set the trip threshold, hysteresis gap, and reset behavior
block.create_stats.security_locker.toolt: A clearance gated safe. Twenty seven slots, a four digit code, and a minute to break into.
Sets into a wall and takes power on any face, so a cable beside it, an Indoor Cable bored through the wall behind it, or an Appliance Cord all feed it. It needs no wire terminal of its own.

No item handler ever: hoppers/funnels/pipes/drains do nothing. Locked: 60s to break with any tool, explosion-proof, tampers on first hit. Broken locked: drops sealed, contents+code intact. Open, or within 10s of closing screen: breaks and spills normally.

Personal: you alone, powered+networked. General: owner + cleared players, open while its screen is up. Else the keypad code. 3 wrong codes: 1-min lock + tamper report. No power/panel: instant lock, evicts everyone, needs the code from all incl. owner. Sneak+use your locker to change type/code.
block.create_stats.sentry_alarm.tooltip: Wireless alarm annunciator with a pixel marquee and rule tiles
Place it within range of what it watches, and keep the block above clear
Scans nearby Stats Display Panels and machines, and shows exactly which rule tripped.
Right-click the panel to set rules; add an antenna to widen its reach
block.create_stats.smart_gearshift.toolt: Redstone preset gearbox for staged RPM changes
Put it inline on a shaft line and drive it with analog redstone 0-15
Redstone-selectable gearbox stage; level 0 passes input through and higher levels shift the shaft to preset RPMs.
A Display Link can read the active stage, target RPM, source RPM, and boost/throttle state
block.create_stats.smart_home_panel.tool: A flush wall panel that finds the appliances on its own circuit and switches them from one screen.
Mounts flush on any wall and takes power on any face, so a cable beside it or an Indoor Cable bored through the wall behind it both feed it. It needs no wire terminal of its own.

Auto-finds lamps, sockets, coffee machines, air fryers, water coolers, ranges, washers on its circuit, stopping at the first PDU/junction. Industrial machines: bind by hand with a Switch Link Card (reaches other circuits). Power's only for the search; unpowered stays dark but works.

Right-click to open. Click a slot, or its mark on the map, to switch it; right-click for brightness, colour and name. Rooms find themselves. Scenes on the hotbar: click an empty slot to save the lights, 1-9 to recall. Click the house name for rules and the wall face.
block.create_stats.stage_light.tooltip.p: Mounts on any face. Right-click to aim and configure.
block.create_stats.stage_light.tooltip.s: Right-click to aim, set range, brightness and focus. Stained glass tints the beam; redstone aims it too.
block.create_stats.stage_light.tooltip.u: Lights the spot it points at, on ships too
block.create_stats.stage_light_mk2.toolt: Mounts on any face. Right-click to configure.
Slot a Beacon to reach 256 blocks; a wrench takes it back out. Stained glass tints the beam.
Lights the spot it points at, on ships too
block.create_stats.stats_alarm.tooltip: Superseded by the Klaxon Alarm and the Sentry Alarm
block.create_stats.stats_alarm.tooltip.p: Kept so existing builds keep working; craft an annunciator instead
block.create_stats.stats_alarm.tooltip.s: Turns on when any channel on a nearby panel reaches its threshold. The annunciators do this with deadbands, acknowledge and per-rule readouts.
block.create_stats.stats_alarm.tooltip.u: Open an annunciator and press Import Alerts to carry its rules across
block.create_stats.stats_display_mk2.too: Next-gen live display with a full-screen configuration studio
Place matching Mk II panels side by side to form a larger multiblock screen
Sneak-right-click to cycle the display mode.
Right-click to open the studio; reads the same sources as the Stats Display Panel
block.create_stats.stats_display_mk3.too: Live instrument panel that redraws every frame
Place matching Mk III panels side by side to form a larger multiblock screen
Sneak-right-click to scrub the plotted time range.
Right-click to open the Mk III studio; reads the same sources, alarms and recorders as every other panel
block.create_stats.stats_display_mk3_con: Standalone console with a raked face, read square on while standing
A single block. Consoles never merge into a multiblock
Sneak-right-click to turn the range knob: 1m, 5m, 15m, all.
Right-click to open the Mk III studio
block.create_stats.stats_display_panel.t: Wall-mounted live display for factory data, graphs, and dashboards
Place matching panels side by side to form a larger multiblock screen
Sneak-right-click to cycle the display mode.
Right-click to open the panel; use a Stats Configurator to copy or paste settings
block.create_stats.stats_recorder.source: Nearby Stats Display - waiting for data
block.create_stats.stats_recorder.toolti: Records incoming Display Link samples for later review
Use it as a Display Link target anywhere you want to log live values
Records Display Link data and copies stored samples into a Memory Cog.
Right-click with empty hand for status, or use a Memory Cog to copy stored samples
block.create_stats.status_tower_light.to: Stackable signal tower for local or linked machine status
Place it above or beside a machine, or feed it with a Display Link; stack up to four for a multi-colour tower

A signal tower that watches up to two neighbouring machines and shows the worse of them. One module is a traffic light, green through amber to red; a stack gives each tier its own fixed colour and lets the flash pattern carry the severity.
Right-click to set source, metric, thresholds, lens colour, alert style and sounder
block.create_stats.strip_lamp.tooltip: A long tube fitting. Tiles into continuous runs along a corridor.
block.create_stats.strip_lamp.tooltip.pl: Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click, and turns to face you. A wrench turns it another quarter.
block.create_stats.strip_lamp.tooltip.sh: Always needs cable power, and no config setting exempts it. A redstone signal switches it off rather than on. Sixteen dye colours are supported.
block.create_stats.strip_lamp.tooltip.us: Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it.
block.create_stats.surface_cable.tooltip: Cable that runs along block faces and turns corners. The starting grade.
block.create_stats.table_alarm_clock.too: Wooden desk clock for game time, stopwatch, timer, and alarm
Set it on a solid top surface like a desk, shelf, or control table
Sneak-right-click the placed clock to stop the ringing fast.
Right-click to switch modes; timer and alarm ring and power redstone until silenced
block.create_stats.tamper_sensor.tooltip: Watches for blocks being broken, placed or blown up nearby.
Mounts on any wall, floor or ceiling and takes power on any face, so a cable beside it or an Indoor Cable bored through the surface behind it both feed it. It needs no wire terminal of its own.
Alarm, not a lock: reports break-ins, can't stop them. Cheapest sensor, never polls. Needs a Home Security Panel on-circuit, no redstone I/O; unpowered = fault, red banner.

Trips when anyone whose clearance does not meet its level breaks or places a block within range, and on any explosion nobody cleared set off. It names the block in the log, so a raid reads as a list of what was taken and from where. Armed by the panel's mode, exactly like a Motion Sensor.
block.create_stats.toaster.tooltip: A two-slot toaster, wired for power rather than plugged in.
block.create_stats.toggle_switch.tooltip: A lever-style switch that reads on or off from across a room.
Place it against any face: it mounts flush on walls, floors and ceilings.
Breaks the cable run it sits in: open the switch and everything downstream goes dark. Also emits redstone.
block.create_stats.topology_scanner.tool: An instrument that sits in a shaft line and maps the kinetic network it turns in.
Put it in a running shaft the way you would a gearshift: rotation passes straight through. It reads the network from wherever it stands, so anywhere on the drivetrain works.

Right-click for a survey: every reachable kinetic element, what drives what, where speed changes, each machine's stress cost. Field grade: 64 elements, layout+speed. Draws its own stress, scaled by grade, shown in survey.
Point a Display Link at it to feed a Stats Display and unlock that panel's Topology tab. A wrench rotates it; cable and wire pass through to the block behind.
block.create_stats.topology_scanner_prob: A clamp-on scanner that grips any kinetic block and runs on Forge Energy instead of stress.
Click it onto the face of the kinetic block you want to measure; the readout ends up facing you. Wire it with a cable, a wire or a cord.

The same survey as the inline Topology Scanner and the same 64-element Field reach, but it takes no rotation and costs no stress: it clamps to a drivetrain from the side and draws FE. Without power it will not scan, and it says so.
Point a Display Link at it to feed a Stats Display and unlock that panel's Topology tab.
block.create_stats.vapour_tight_lamp.too: A sealed batten for anywhere wet, dusty or cold.
Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click, and turns to face you. A wrench turns it another quarter.
Always needs cable power, and no config setting exempts it. A redstone signal switches it off rather than on. Sixteen dye colours are supported.
Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it.
block.create_stats.vcc_mk2.tooltip: The polished gold successor to the Vehicle Control Computer, with a live CRT flight deck
block.create_stats.vcc_mk2.tooltip.place: Place on a Sable contraption; the screen shows a live glass-cockpit readout
block.create_stats.vcc_mk2.tooltip.shift: Work in progress: the full control interface is coming in a later update
block.create_stats.vcc_mk2.tooltip.usage: Right-click to cycle the screen state while the new interface is built
block.create_stats.vcc_mk3.tooltip.summa: Reads your craft's real sensors, drives your hardware through RPM Governors, and tells you exactly what is still unlinked
block.create_stats.vcc_mk3.tooltip.usage: Right-click to open the console. Link hardware with Propeller and Governor Cards, fit it onto the craft on RIG, then arm it to fly
block.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tooltip: One console for any ground vehicle: finds its wheels, governors, jets, swivel bearings, machines and lights, and drives them from the seat
block.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tooltip.place: Build it into a physics craft, facing the way the vehicle goes: its instrument panel then faces the seat. It finds every Offroad wheel mount, RPM Governor, propeller, swivel bearing and Redstone Link receiver on the craft, and on trailers or halves joined to it by swivel bearings. A governor drives whatever its shaft line turns
block.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tooltip.shift: Its desk shows the drive: the wheel turns with the steering, the throttle and brake levers follow what the wheels are given, the needle reads km/h (one block a metre), and lamps show the brakes, the hold, reverse, the indicators, boost and a route driving.
block.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tooltip.usage: Right-click for the console: steering, keys, jets, tools, lights and every part it found. Sit in a seat within 2 blocks of the console and drive (two can drive at once): W/S, A/D, Space brakes, Sprint fires the jets, Z/X/C work the tools. Every key can be rebound on the console
block.create_stats.vcc_mk4_aerial.toolti: Flies a zeppelin from the seat: holds its altitude through the burners and its speed and heading through the props, learns what its wings and engines do to its height, and never drops it

Build it into a physics craft, facing the ship's nose. It finds the Hot Air Burners and Steam Vents under every balloon and every propeller an RPM Governor turns, and learns their gearing the first time they spin

Sit in a seat within 2 blocks of the Aerial to fly (two pilots at once): W and S ring the telegraph (Full, Half and Slow Astern, Stop, Slow, Half and Full Ahead), A and D turn, Space and X move the altitude held. Use it for its console: the bridge, every balloon, engine, fin, tool and light, and the keys. Stand up in the air and it anchors, keeps its course or flies to the Navigation Table's target; sneak and use it with an empty hand to step through them. A Display Link reads it to a Stats Display Mk III
block.create_stats.vcc_mk4_aerial_flight: VCC Mk IV Aerial Flight Deck
The VCC Mk IV Aerial, two blocks wide: a captain and a first officer side by side, each with a yoke and the full six, the throttles, the trim wheel and the compass between them
Place it facing the ship's nose: the first officer's half goes on your right, and that block must be free. It flies the ship exactly as the Aerial does, and a craft takes one of them

Sit behind either half to fly (two pilots at once), with the Aerial's keys: W and S ring the telegraph, A and D turn, Space and X move the altitude held. Use either half for the console; sneak and use it with an empty hand to choose what the ship does without a pilot in the air. A Display Link reads it from either half
block.create_stats.vehicle_light_white.t: Headlight or reverse light. Throws a beam of light where it points.
Lit by a VCC Mk IV on the same vehicle, or by redstone: a weak signal is the dipped beam, a full one the full beam
Sticks to any face with the lens outward. A wrench turns it.
A VCC Mk IV finds it with no frequency to set. Pointing forward it becomes a headlight, lit while you drive; pointing back, a reverse light. Its beam lights the road on a moving Sable craft too.
block.create_stats.vehicle_light_red.too: Tail light and brake light in one lamp.
Dim on a weak signal (the tail light), bright on a full one (the brake light). A VCC Mk IV drives it as both
Sticks to any face with the lens outward. A wrench turns it.
A VCC Mk IV finds it with no frequency to set and picks Tail and brake: dim while you drive, bright while the wheels brake.
block.create_stats.vehicle_light_amber.t: Turn signal. Flashes by itself while powered.
Any signal makes it flash, so a lever makes it a hazard light. A VCC Mk IV drives it as an indicator
Sticks to any face with the lens outward. A wrench turns it.

A VCC Mk IV finds it with no frequency to set and picks the indicator for its side: left of the vehicle's centre line it flashes when you steer left, right of it when you steer right. Every signal on a vehicle flashes in step.
block.create_stats.wall_sconce.tooltip: A half-shaded sconce that washes light up a wall.
block.create_stats.wall_sconce.tooltip.p: Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click, and turns to face you. A wrench turns it another quarter.
block.create_stats.wall_sconce.tooltip.s: Always needs cable power, and no config setting exempts it. A redstone signal switches it off rather than on. Sixteen dye colours are supported.
block.create_stats.wall_sconce.tooltip.u: Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it.
block.create_stats.bankers_lamp.tooltip: A desk lamp: a black shade on a brass arm and column, a filament bulb under it and a pull chain.
Stands on any face and turns to face you. A wrench turns it another quarter.
Always needs cable power, and no config setting exempts it. A redstone signal switches it off rather than on. Sixteen dye colours are supported.
Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it. Dims in ten steps from a Rotary Dimmer or the Smart Home Panel.
block.create_stats.water_cooler.tooltip: A plumbed break-room cooler with three taps.
Pipe water to the flange on the back and wire the studs below it for power.
Spring runs on water alone; Chilled needs the compressor at temperature; Sparkling needs that and a charged carbonator.
Hold a mug under a tap. The plain tap also fills Buckets and Glass Bottles.
block.create_stats.cine_camera.tooltip: A tracking camera on a steel tripod: it follows one thing and measures it.
block.create_stats.cine_camera.tooltip.p: Two blocks tall. Placed facing the way you look, with you standing where its operator stands.
block.create_stats.cine_camera.tooltip.u: Right-click to look through it. It runs on a battery that films for an hour, charged from a cable or an Appliance Cord to its tripod's foot, and keeps its charge when broken. Sneak and right-click to change mode. A Display Link reads its measurements.
block.create_stats.cine_camera.tooltip.s: In Film mode, left-click records a video into the cine_films folder, and the inventory key opens the camera's menu: frame rate, resolution, quality and frame. Step out mid-take and it keeps filming until the Record / Stop key (R) stops it.
block.create_stats.water_sensor.tooltip: Watches for water at or below itself. Never switches off.
Mounts on any wall, floor or ceiling and takes power on any face, so a cable beside it or an Indoor Cable bored through the surface behind it both feed it. It needs no wire terminal of its own.

Hazard sensor: ignores house mode, no lockdown, no doors touched. Logs the trip, ambers the panel's banner+face, clears 10s later. Good over cellars, fluid networks, burst-prone pipes. Needs a Home Security Panel on-circuit, no redstone I/O; unpowered = fault, red banner.

Trips on water or flowing fluid within range, measured downward and outward rather than in every direction: water falls, so a flood sensor that watched its own height would only fire once the room had already filled to it. Mount it high and it still sees the floor.
block.create_stats.weather_panel.tooltip: A flush wall panel that reads the sky, and the countdown timers behind it.
Mounts flush on any wall, powers from any face (cable or Indoor Cable), no wire terminal needed. Temperature from biome, pressure from altitude: mountains read colder/lower than valleys.
Reads live rain/thunder countdowns for a sure near forecast, then sims ahead for days 2-5 (odds, not a promise). Draws 1 FE/t. Unpowered: dark, but the screen still opens and shows reading age.
Face shows condition, temperature, countdown to next change. Right-click: live sky, 5-day forecast, tendency barometer, temp curve. C/F chip is per-player, follows you anywhere.
block.create_stats.well_glass_lamp.toolt: Cast brass and a thick globe under a hooped guard.
Place it against any face: it points away from whatever you click, and turns to face you. A wrench turns it another quarter.
Always needs cable power, and no config setting exempts it. A redstone signal switches it off rather than on. Sixteen dye colours are supported.
Lights whenever its cable is feeding it. Right-click with any dye to recolour it.
block.create_stats.window_shutter.toolti: A powered shutter that fills a window opening. Two leaves that meet in the middle, at any height up to 8 blocks.

Click a 1x2 opening to center, or a wall face for a flush 6px mount. Wrench cycles the 3 mounts, sneak-wrench sets a whole bank. Hold one, look at a column to grow it, up to 8 tall. Adjacent same-height columns link into one bank. Powers from any face: cable, Indoor Cable, or Appliance Cord.

No hand release, redstone I/O, or clearance, ever. Whole bank charges before moving, so an unpaid bank stays put, never half-seals. Taller = slower, costlier, bigger buffer. No power holds position; open, leaves stow fully clear.

3 triggers: lockdown seals every shutter, panel toggle seals one bank, dusk flag closes at night/opens dawn. Fire release forces every shutter open, beats both. Click with a shutter in hand: grows it a block taller.
block.create_stats.wire_terminal_junctio: A terminal strip for Copper Wire: six studs in three pairs, three separate circuits.
Mount it on any sturdy wall face, then run one wire to each stud you want on a circuit

Separate is the default and the reason to own one: A is the left pair, B the middle, C the right, and power crosses between them nowhere. Merged puts every stud on one bus, for a distribution point rather than a pass through.
Open the door and flip the lever to tie all six studs into one bus; the handle on the right flank isolates the whole strip
