create_stats.jei.air_fryer.info:
A countertop convection fryer that runs on the grid rather than on fuel. It takes every furnace smelting recipe, holds eight of one thing in its basket, and cooks the lot on one press of the start button.

It is fast at food and deliberately slow at everything else: food cooks in 45% of the time a furnace would take, and anything that is not food takes 140% of it. Smelting ore in here works and is meant to be a joke rather than a plan - the Induction Smelter does the same ore over three times faster and for a third of the power.

Cooking draws 64 FE/t and standing switched on draws 4 FE/t. There is no fuel slot and no internal battery worth the name: if the grid cannot carry the load the countdown pauses and holds where it stopped rather than losing the batch, which is what the frozen clock on the front is telling you.

A hopper on top feeds raw food in, a hopper underneath takes cooked food out, and a redstone pulse presses start. Power goes into the terminal on the back, and only the back.
create_stats.jei.air_frying.basket_note: One basket is %s of a single item and one press of start. It will not take a mixed load, and it will not start again until the cooked food is out.
create_stats.jei.air_frying.draw_note: %1$s FE/t while cooking, and %2$s FE/t for as long as the mains rocker is on. The figures above are the cooking draw only.
create_stats.jei.air_frying.lane_bulk_no: Not food, so it runs slower than a furnace would on purpose. If this is ore, the Induction Smelter is over three times faster and three times cheaper - this lane exists so the block does not have to refuse things, not because it is good at them.
create_stats.jei.air_frying.lane_food_no: Food is what this block is for: quicker than a Smoker, eight at a time, and no fuel at all.
create_stats.jei.arc_smelting.slag: Only on a run that could not hold its arc. Steady the grid and you never see it.
create_stats.jei.biofuel_burner.info: Makes %1$s FE/t from plant matter: any wood, leaves, saplings, flowers, crops, or anything a composter takes. What you feed it sets how long it runs, never how hard. Coal and blaze rods are refused. It pauses while its %2$s FE buffer is full. Power leaves the back and both sides. The Fuel page lists what burns for how long.
create_stats.jei.blast_shutter.info:
A powered shutter for a window opening: stand it in the hole, or hang it flush on the wall over it. A 1 by 2 hole takes one shutter: the upper leaf travels down from the top of it, the lower one up from the bottom, and they meet in the middle.

It grows. Hold another shutter, look at one you have already placed, and the next block of that column is ghosted in at whichever end you are aiming at; clicking puts it there, one item per block, up to 8 blocks tall. Nothing about the housing had to change to allow it: a stowed leaf is every slat at the same height inside four pixels of case, so four pixels hides thirty of them as readily as six. A taller column is slower to seal and costs more to move, and its buffer grows to match.

Open, both leaves are stowed in four pixels of housing and you see straight through. That is the point of the block: a shutter that blocked the view when open would be a wall with extra steps.

Where it sits in its own block is a choice, and the block is sixteen pixels deep while the housing is six. Clicking the side of a block mounts it flush against that wall and looking away from it, which is what a shutter over a window looks like; clicking a floor or a ceiling centres it in the opening, which is what a shutter in a window looks like. A wrench cycles a placed column between centred, flush front and flush back, and sneak-wrenching gives a whole bank the mount of the column you aimed at. Nothing else changes with it: the same travel, the same slats, the same cost, the same leaves meeting in the same place.

A contiguous run at the same level, of the same height in blocks, facing the same way and of the same tier, links into one bank. A bank is one row on the panel, one decision, one sound and one charge. Every unit is tested before any unit is charged, so a bank that cannot pay for the move stays where it is rather than sealing half of an opening.

Three triggers and no others. A lockdown seals every shutter on the panel. The panel's own toggle seals one bank by choice, and that is not a lockdown: it raises no banner and clearing a lockdown does not undo it. The dusk flag, set per bank, closes it at nightfall and opens it at dawn, so a bedroom can shutter itself while the workshop stays open.

A fire release opens every shutter and beats both of the others. A window is a smoke vent and an escape route, and sealing a burning building is the exact failure that release exists to prevent. Unlike the doors there is no entrance exception, because nobody walks in through a window they had to have already reached.

There is no hand release, no redstone in or out, and no clearance. A shutter is never something you walk up to, so there is nothing on it for a clearance to open.

Two tiers. The Window Shutter is light, ordinary blast resistance, and seals in a little over half a second. The Blast Shutter is armoured, takes an iron pickaxe, survives any explosion in the game, and takes a full second. Both cost the same to move: pricing the tier twice would make the better shutter a trap rather than a choice.
create_stats.jei.bread_slicer.info:
A countertop slicer, one blade that never stops, cutting a loaf into four, six or eight slices at the same feed rate every time. Thinner slices mean more, faster strokes over the same eight second pass, not a slower loaf.

The draw doubles at every notch rather than scaling with the stroke count: 20 FE/t at four slices, 40 at six, 80 at eight. So the cost per slice rises too, from 800 FE at the coarsest setting to about 1,070 at the middle and 1,600 at the finest, and asking for thin slices is a real decision rather than a free preference. The lever is refused mid pass, because changing the rate partway through would cut the slices already done a different thickness from the ones still to come.

The lid is the interlock. It will not run with the lid up, and lifting it mid pass pauses the cut rather than losing it, exactly like a power failure would. Taking the loaf out by hand is the only way to abandon a pass, and doing that hands back the loaf and whatever slices were already cut.

A hopper above feeds loaves in, a hopper below takes slices out, and nothing else on the machine does. A comparator reads how full the delivery end is. Power lands on the back, and only the back.
create_stats.jei.bulk_washer.info:
A one-block replacement for the Encased Fan and its column of water. It runs Create's splashing recipe list unchanged, which means every ore-washing recipe in the pack, and every recipe an addon or datapack registers, works in it on the day it is added.

The drum holds 256 items counted across all stacks, and each item in it is either waiting or washed. Only washed items leave, whether through the door or through the output funnel, so a machine that is mid-load never hands back half-finished work.

Three programmes trade power against throughput. Eco washes 16 items every 10 seconds at 8 FE/t, Half 32 every 7 seconds at 46 FE/t, and Full 64 every 5 seconds at 256 FE/t. Standing switched on with the drum still costs 4 FE/t. Water is a flat 20 mB per item in every programme, out of a 3,000 mB internal tank: fill it with a bucket on any face, or pipe it into the back.

Four faces do automation and they do different jobs. The back is the services face: the terminal studs, the hose boss, and a way in for items, so a machine against a wall can be wired, plumbed and fed through the one side nobody walks past. The underside is the drain: water in, washed items out, and never items in, so a hopper under the machine collects from it rather than feeding it. The two flanks carry the belt ports drawn on them, one in and one out. The front door takes no automation at all. A comparator reads how full the drum is, so a line feeding the machine can tell whether it may send more.

Starving it never costs you the load. If power, water or the mains go away, the drum stops where it is, the amber lamp lights, and the countdown holds until you fix it.
create_stats.jei.drum_washing.dial_note: Eco is the cheapest per item and the slowest, Full is the fastest and the dearest, and Half sits between them. What Full charges you for is throughput rather than time.
create_stats.jei.drum_washing.draw_note: %1$s to %2$s FE/t while the drum turns, and %3$s FE/t for as long as the mains is on. The figures above are the washing draw only.
create_stats.jei.drum_washing.water_note: Water is a flat %1$s mB per item in all three programmes, out of a %2$s mB tank: about %3$s items on a full one. Top it up with a bucket on any face, or pipe water into the back.
create_stats.jei.drum_washing.yield_gain: This one hands back more than it took. The drum's %s items are waiting and washed counted together, so a full load of this fills itself from the inside and stops taking new work until the washed side is cleared.
create_stats.jei.drum_washing.yield_note: The drum's %s items are waiting and washed counted together, so it only takes a fresh load once there is room for one.
create_stats.jei.fire_sensor.info:
Watches for fire, lava, a lit campfire, or any creature that is burning.

This is a HAZARD sensor, so it ignores the house mode completely and is watching in every one of them. There is no setting that turns it off, because a smoke alarm that can be switched off is a broken smoke alarm. A hazard never raises a lockdown either: locking every door in a burning building is the opposite of the right answer.

What it does instead is the mirror image of a lockdown: a trip RELEASES every door on the panel, so they open for anyone, and it beats a standing lockdown, because a burning house outranks a burgled one. The door marked as the ENTRANCE is the single exception and stays owner only, so a fire set outside is never a way in through your front door.

The release lapses on its own ten seconds after the last sighting, so nobody has to come and clear it. The one state that exists because the building is on fire is the one state that must not require a trip to the panel.

It reports to a Home Security Panel on the same circuit and does nothing without one. These emit no redstone by design, so the whole security system stays one closed loop with a single place to reason about it: the panel decides, the sensor only ever says what it saw.

It draws 1 FE/t and holds ten seconds of buffer, so a grid dip does not blind the house. An unpowered sensor is not a degraded sensor, it is one that has stopped watching, so the panel counts it as a fault and turns its banner red rather than letting the house look secure while nothing is looking at it.
create_stats.jei.garage_door.info:
A roller shutter that sizes itself. Lay a run of Garage Door Hoods along the top of an opening and the curtain hangs out of them on its own.

The run is the width. Hold a hood, look at one you have already placed, and the next along the run is ghosted in for you already facing the right way, which matters more than it sounds: a run only counts as one door while every hood in it faces the same way. Up to twelve of them.

The drop is whatever there is room for, measured every couple of seconds against the world, up to twelve blocks. Park a crate under one corner and the whole door shortens to clear it, because a bottom bar is one rigid extrusion and cannot come down in a staircase. Move the crate and it reaches the floor again.

Twelve is a cap with a reason you can see. The curtain winds onto a barrel inside the hood, that barrel fattens as it takes up curtain, and the hood is drawn at exactly the diameter a fully wound one reaches. A thirteen block curtain would not fit inside the drum you are looking at.

Four ways to work it, and the first two are the point of it. It opens for a PLAYER within range who is allowed through, and for a VEHICLE driving at it, which is a box the size of the opening projected out both ways rather than a sphere, so a minecart passing along the outside wall does not open every bay on it. It also takes a REDSTONE signal at any hood, and a CLICK on any hood or curtain block. An unmanned contraption is refused unless you allow it with a wrench, so nothing can drive itself into a locked bay.

It closes itself five seconds after the last thing that opened it goes away, and it REVERSES if anything is standing in the doorway while it comes down. That is not decoration: the curtain becomes passable row by row as it rises and it accelerates on the way down, so a closing door genuinely can come down on somebody.

A Home Security Panel on the same circuit governs it like any other door: a clearance to open it, a lockdown that seals it, a fire release that opens it, and it can be named as the one ENTRANCE a sealed house is re-entered by.

Power is taken on any face of any hood, or through a wall by boring a cable into one. It costs %s FE per block of curtain per move, charged in full the instant the move starts, so a door either opens or declines and never stops half way. It idles at one FE per tick for every %s blocks of curtain, and holds %s moves in its buffer.
create_stats.jei.home_security_panel.inf:
A wall keypad that decides who may use the security devices on its own circuit.

It finds them the same way the Smart Home Panel finds appliances: along its own wiring, stopping at the first Power Distribution Unit, Wire Terminal Junction or Battery Controller it reaches. So one panel covers one circuit, and the way to get a panel per wing is to end that wing's wiring at a junction box. A Switch Link Card binds a device that is not on the circuit at all, which is the universal override in both directions.

Two separate things decide what somebody can do. A CLEARANCE from 1 to 5 says what they may open: a device passes them when their clearance is at or above the level it asks for. A ROLE says what they may change: an Owner edits everything, an Admin edits the roster and the levels but cannot touch the Owner or grant a clearance above their own, and a Member changes nothing. Keeping them apart is the point, so handing somebody the vault key never also hands them the ability to write themselves a new one.

Whoever places the panel is the Owner, and the Owner passes every device regardless of level. That is a check of its own rather than a sixth clearance, so it survives every level in the house being changed.

The Access view draws every person against every device at once, which is the only place a permissions mistake reads as a shape rather than as a number you have to go and check.

It draws %s FE/t, and that pays for the search alone. Losing power stops it finding anything new; it never stops you changing what it has already found.
create_stats.jei.induction_smelter.info:
Smelts and blasts at belt volume, fifteen percent faster than the furnace or blast furnace it replaces, and burns no fuel at all - the grid is its fuel.

Rate follows temperature, so a half-warm muffle runs at half speed and every duration quoted here is the figure at full heat. The damper sets how hot it is allowed to get: Shut is off, Half caps at 70% and runs the smelting lane only, Open is full temperature and opens the blasting lane above four fifths of it.

Touching Smelters pool into one machine. A bank shares its power and its item routing, so one cable landing anywhere on a wall feeds all of it and one funnel each side loads and unloads the lot. Heat stays per module, which is what lets an underfed wall right-size itself: the modules nobody is asking for work go cold and stop billing.

Power goes into the conduit gland on the back, and only the back.
create_stats.jei.induction_smelting.cold: Warming a cold muffle costs a further %s FE over about %s seconds, before a single piece moves.
create_stats.jei.induction_smelting.hold: Holding temperature between pieces costs %s FE/t, so a steady feed is what this machine charges you for.
create_stats.jei.induction_smelting.lane: The blasting lane only opens above four fifths of full temperature, which the Half detent caps below. This one needs the damper open.
Runs on any detent that lets the muffle warm at all. If this item also has a blasting recipe, an open damper will take that faster lane instead.
create_stats.jei.motion_sensor.info:
Watches for people without clearance, and for anything hostile, within its range.

The test is the same one every door in the mod runs: a player passes when their clearance on the panel's roster is at or above the level the panel sets for this sensor, and a player who passes walks by without tripping it.

Hostile mobs always trip it, on the grounds that a creeper approaching your walls is precisely when you want the doors shut. Everything else alive is ignored: an animal, a villager, an iron golem you built or an armour stand you placed is not an intruder, and a sensor that treated them as one would sit in a permanent trip and seal the house the moment you armed it.

Range runs from 2 to 16 blocks and is set per sensor from the panel's Sensors tab.

The panel's mode decides whether it is armed. AT HOME forces every intrusion sensor to log only. AWAY arms all of them. AT HOME, ARMED reads each sensor's own switch, which is the only mode where that switch means anything.

A trip while armed puts the house into LOCKDOWN: every door on the panel shuts and refuses everyone, the owner included. The way back in is the one door marked as the ENTRANCE, which opens for the owner alone until the lockdown is cleared at the panel. That rule is what makes a lockdown recoverable instead of a way to permanently lose your own base, and it means the intruder who tripped it is sealed inside rather than merely being made a noise at.

It draws 1 FE/t and holds ten seconds of buffer, so a grid dip does not blind the house. An unpowered sensor is not a degraded sensor, it is one that has stopped watching, so the panel counts it as a fault and turns its banner red rather than letting the house look secure while nothing is looking at it.
create_stats.jei.powered_door.info:
A two-tall door that runs on Forge Energy and can be handed over to a Home Security Panel.

POWER. It holds %s FE, draws %s FE/t standing and spends %s FE the instant it starts an open or a close. The whole cycle is charged up front, so a door that cannot afford the travel declines to start rather than stopping half way across its own doorway. It takes power on any face of either of its blocks, and it is a bore socket: point a Cable Bore at the jamb or the lintel with a run behind it and the sleeve comes through, so the wiring stays inside the wall instead of round the door.

DISCOVERY. A Home Security Panel finds every door on its own circuit with nothing to configure, and gives each one a required clearance from 1 to 5. A player passes when their clearance meets it, and the owner passes everything. Until a panel claims a door, it opens for anyone.

PROXIMITY. Set a radius on the panel and a door opens for anyone who clears it as they walk up, and shuts again behind them. A door you opened by hand stays open until you shut it.

WHEN THINGS BREAK. Each door keeps its own copy of the roster, so it goes on refusing when the panel is unpowered, unloaded or destroyed. With no power the motor will not run at all: redstone and proximity both stop working, and whether a hand can still shift the leaf is the panel's fail secure setting.

MATERIALS. Nine, and they do not all move the same way. Iron swings, slides and does both pair motions. Reinforced never swings, because a blast leaf on hinges is a blast leaf with hinges to blow. Quartz is the residential one and folds itself into a pocket. The six wood species fold three different ways, because a wooden bi-fold is a real thing and a steel one is not.

PAIRS. Two doors side by side become a double door when their hinges face outward, and then they move as one leaf in two halves. Sneak plus a wrench flips a hinge, which is how you make one. Sneak plus an empty hand toggles an interlocked toothed seam between the two.
create_stats.jei.security_locker.info:
A clearance gated safe with twenty seven slots, and the first thing in the mod that the 1 to 5 clearance ladder actually opens.

The first time its owner opens one, a locker asks whose it is, and the answer decides everything below. A general locker is the household's and runs on the clearance ladder. A personal locker is one player's: it opens for the person who placed it and for nobody else, whatever the roster says and whoever owns the house, and everybody else types its code. It recognises its holder only while it has power and a panel, so off the network the code is the only way in, its holder included. The code is set at the block, by the holder, when they choose personal, and the panel is refused the control entirely: an admin who could write a code onto a personal locker could open it a moment later. Sneak and use your own locker to change the answer or the code. Mining it is the only other way in, and it takes a minute under an alarm.

Two ways in, and either one is enough. The owner of the Home Security Panel always opens it, and so does anybody whose clearance on the roster meets the level the panel sets for this locker. Everybody else gets a keypad: the four digit code opens it for that visit whatever the roster says, which is how you let somebody into one box without putting them on the list.

The code is set from the panel's Lockers tab, by the owner or an admin, and it is write only. The panel never shows an existing code back, not even to the owner, because an admin who can read every code in the house is a second owner by another route.

Three wrong codes in a row shut that locker's keypad for sixty seconds and report tamper to the panel, which in an armed house is a lockdown. Ten thousand combinations at three tries a minute is about two days of typing, and there is no way to speed it up.

Nothing can automate it. There is no item handler on any face in any state, so hoppers, funnels, pipes and Create's item drains do nothing at all, in or out.

The reader needs both power and the panel. Lose either one and the locker shuts on the spot, puts whoever was looking inside out of it, and asks everybody for the code, the owner included -- and it goes on asking after the power comes back, until somebody answers it. The code still opens it throughout, so a grid failure can never lock you out of your own storage, and that is what makes the code worth remembering. If the reader dies on a locker that never had a code, the keypad turns around and lets the first person there set one, because nobody can be asked for a password that was never chosen.

Locked, it takes exactly sixty seconds to break with any tool at any enchantment level, and no explosion touches it. The minute is not the defence: the first tick of mining reports tamper to the panel, and the alarm during that minute is. When it finally gives way it drops sealed, still holding its contents and its code, so breaking a locker moves the problem rather than solving it. Standing open it breaks like any other container and spills, which is how you pick up your own storage without unloading it first.
create_stats.jei.smart_home_panel.info:
A wall remote for the appliances on its own circuit.

It discovers them by itself, and where it stops looking is the point. The search follows this panel's own wiring and ends at the first Power Distribution Unit, Wire Terminal Junction or Battery Controller it reaches, exactly where every circuit in the mod ends. So one panel covers one circuit, and the way to get a panel per room is to end each room's wiring at a junction box, which is what a breaker box is for in a real house.

Lamps, Power Outlets, Coffee Machines, Air Fryers, Water Coolers, Induction Ranges and Bulk Washers are found without being asked. Motors, Arc Furnaces, Induction Smelters and Fluid Pumps never are: those are industrial, and a Switch Link Card is the only way onto the panel for them. The card also reaches fixtures on other circuits entirely, so it is the universal override in both directions.

Rows carry a bearing and a distance, and hovering one outlines the actual block through the wall, which is how you tell four identical lamps apart. Lamps of one kind that touch each other collapse into a single row with one switch and one dimmer, because a corridor is ten fittings and ten rows is a list nobody reads.

It draws %s FE/t, and that pays for the search alone. Losing power stops it finding anything new; it never stops you switching what it has already found.
create_stats.jei.tamper_sensor.info:
Watches for blocks being broken, blocks being placed, and explosions.

It is an alarm, not a claim system. It never stops anyone breaking anything; it tells you that they did, and it names the block, so a raid reads in the panel's log as a list of what was taken and from where. Anyone whose clearance meets the sensor's level can rearrange their own house without tripping it, and that includes blasting: an explosion is attributed to whoever lit it, so your own TNT in your own cellar does not seal the house, and a creeper's charge, which nobody lit, always counts.

It is also the cheapest of the four to run. The other three look at the world on a clock; this one never polls at all and costs nothing until something actually happens.

The panel's mode decides whether it is armed. AT HOME forces every intrusion sensor to log only. AWAY arms all of them. AT HOME, ARMED reads each sensor's own switch, which is the only mode where that switch means anything.

A trip while armed puts the house into LOCKDOWN: every door on the panel shuts and refuses everyone, the owner included. The way back in is the one door marked as the ENTRANCE, which opens for the owner alone until the lockdown is cleared at the panel. That rule is what makes a lockdown recoverable instead of a way to permanently lose your own base, and it means the intruder who tripped it is sealed inside rather than merely being made a noise at.

It reports to a Home Security Panel on the same circuit and does nothing without one. These emit no redstone by design, so the whole security system stays one closed loop with a single place to reason about it: the panel decides, the sensor only ever says what it saw.

It draws 1 FE/t and holds ten seconds of buffer, so a grid dip does not blind the house. An unpowered sensor is not a degraded sensor, it is one that has stopped watching, so the panel counts it as a fault and turns its banner red rather than letting the house look secure while nothing is looking at it.
create_stats.jei.toaster.info:
Two slots on one lever: both carriages drop and rise together, because a two-slice toaster has one lever, not two independent lanes.

Seven detents pick from five browning stages, light to well done, and the cycle length is what actually changes: 2.5 seconds at the lightest setting up to 7.3 at the darkest. Toasting draws 80 FE/t with all four elements lit. The bagel setting energises only the two inner elements, half the panels for half the draw, 40 FE/t, and browns one side while the other stays soft. Standing by costs 2 FE/t, the least of any appliance on the roster, because a mechanical cam and a latch solenoid are the only things drawing power when nothing is toasting.

Losing power, being shed by a Power Distribution Unit or being switched off from a Smart Home Panel all leave the carriage down and the browning exactly where it stopped; the elements go cold and the countdown holds rather than losing the batch.

Bread goes in the top, toast comes out the bottom, so a hopper above and a hopper below make it a belt machine. A comparator reads how many finished slices are waiting. Power lands on the back, and only the back.
create_stats.jei.water_sensor.info:
Watches for water and flowing fluid at or below its own height.

Downward, not in every direction, and that is the whole design: water falls, so a flood sensor that watched its own level would only fire once the room had already filled to the height of the sensor, which is the point at which you have noticed by other means. Mount it high on a cellar wall and it is still watching the floor.

Useful over a basement, a Create fluid network, or anything with a pipe in it that can burst.

This is a HAZARD sensor, so it ignores the house mode completely and is watching in every one of them. There is no setting that turns it off, because a smoke alarm that can be switched off is a broken smoke alarm. A hazard never raises a lockdown either: locking every door in a burning building is the opposite of the right answer.

It reports to a Home Security Panel on the same circuit and does nothing without one. These emit no redstone by design, so the whole security system stays one closed loop with a single place to reason about it: the panel decides, the sensor only ever says what it saw.

It draws 1 FE/t and holds ten seconds of buffer, so a grid dip does not blind the house. An unpowered sensor is not a degraded sensor, it is one that has stopped watching, so the panel counts it as a fault and turns its banner red rather than letting the house look secure while nothing is looking at it.
create_stats.jei.weather_panel.info:
A wall station that reads the weather, and the part of it the game normally hides.

Minecraft does not schedule weather far ahead, but it is not unknowable either. The server keeps live countdowns to the next rain and the next thunder, and they run independently of each other, so at any moment there is a stretch of time whose weather is already decided. The panel reads those counters and draws that stretch with hard edges and an exact time. That part is not a guess.

Past it, the panel runs the game's own weather machine forward a few hundred times from the state it is in now and counts how many of those futures rain. So days two to five carry a real chance of rain rather than an invented one, and today carries no percentage at all, because today is already settled.

Temperature, humidity and pressure are read from where the panel is standing: the biome sets the baseline, rain pulls it down, the time of day swings it, and a desert swings further than a jungle. Pressure falls with height at about 1 hPa per nine blocks, so two panels in one base can legitimately disagree.

One world rain reads three ways depending on the wall it is bolted to: rain, snow where it is cold enough, and dry in a desert where nothing falls at all. That last one is a real fact about your spot that nothing else in the game will tell you.

It draws %s FE/t and shows only. Losing power darkens the face; the screen still opens and says how stale the reading is.
create_stats.jei.portable_power_interfac:
Create's portable interface, for Forge Energy. Put one on a train or any contraption, facing out, and one at the station, facing the track, up to two blocks apart. When the train stops, the two reach for each other and power moves between the station's circuit and the Capacitor Banks the train carries.

Hold right-click on the station block's rate box to set it. The green top row charges the train; the amber bottom row draws power back out of it. The column is the speed, from %s to %s. The station block's lamp shows the same colour while it works, so a docked pair reads from across the platform.

The percentage box is the charge the interface always leaves behind on the side power is coming from. Charging, that is the station's Capacitor Banks: the ones on its own circuit, or, behind a Power Distribution Unit or Battery Controller, the ones that board spends. A docked train cannot empty the station. Drawing, it is the train's banks. A station with no banks has nothing to protect and charges from generation alone.

On a Power Distribution Unit the interface is a Low priority load by default, so a charging train is the first thing shed in a shortage, and it waits while the board feeding the station is short. A train it draws from counts as supply for the panel. On a Battery Controller, charge from an output and draw into an input. On a panel's leg, draw from ahead of any Power Limiter, never past one. Redstone switches it off. A comparator reads the docked train's charge, 1 to 15.

A train waits only as long as its schedule says. Add the Train charge condition to wait for a percentage. Any other contraption stays docked until it is full, empty or held by the floor, then moves on a few seconds later. Two interfaces docked to one train in opposite directions will not pass power between each other: the first one working keeps the train.
create_stats.load_balancer.hint.balancin: Trimming both branches to hold them inside the stress band.

create_stats.load_balancer.hint.disabled: Balancing is switched off, so both branches run at full source speed.
create_stats.load_balancer.hint.idle: Feed rotation into the rear shaft to wake it up.
create_stats.load_balancer.hint.merged: The two branches rejoin downstream. Keep the left and right networks separate.
create_stats.load_balancer.hint.no_branc: Attach a shaft to the left or right output face.
create_stats.load_balancer.hint.one_bran: One output face is bare. Attach a shaft there, or ignore this if a single branch is intended.
create_stats.load_balancer.hint.pass_thr: Rear shaft is the input; the left and right shafts are controlled outputs.
create_stats.load_balancer.hint.topology: The branch scan hit the node cap, so these figures are incomplete. Simplify the network.
create_stats.load_balancer.hint.wrong_in: Power is arriving on an output face. The rear face must be the source.

create_stats.book.power_meter.applicatio: Place it against the machine and the gland turns to face it. A wrench turns it later.
create_stats.book.power_meter.function.t: Supply end. Its face is engraved below it.
create_stats.book.power_meter.function.g: Load end. Its face is engraved below it.

create_stats.book.power_meter.status.idl: Wired at both ends; nothing is crossing.
create_stats.book.power_meter.status.bac: Full: the load is not taking what is offered.
create_stats.book.power_meter.status.no_: Nothing on the brass terminal can supply.

create_stats.book.power_meter.status.loo: One circuit reaches both terminals. Refused: it would count the same FE forever.

create_stats.book.how_to_read.title: How to read a data sheet
create_stats.book.how_to_read.hook: Every sheet has the same parts in the same places. Here they are, pinned.
create_stats.book.how_to_read.caption: The Power Meter's spread, drawn small.
The section's number and name on the left, what kind of sheet it is on the right.
create_stats.book.how_to_read.part.ribbo: Hangs over the sheet you last closed the book at. The book opens there.
create_stats.book.how_to_read.part.title: Title
The block's name as the game prints it, its registry id, and one line on the idea.
One per section. In a spread, the sections you have passed stand out on the left. Click one for its contents.
create_stats.book.how_to_read.part.figur: The machine's real screen, drawn live. Each numbered pin names one control.
create_stats.book.how_to_read.part.ratin: Figures read from the mod's code as the page is drawn, each marked with a plus.
create_stats.book.how_to_read.part.appli: A usual build from supply to load, this block framed.
create_stats.book.how_to_read.part.see_a: Sheets worth reading next, with their page numbers. Click one to turn there.
create_stats.book.how_to_read.part.contr: What each pinned control does, numbered like its pin. Point at either and both light.
create_stats.book.how_to_read.part.statu: Every word the machine can show, with its mark and what it means.
create_stats.book.how_to_read.part.fault: One question at a time. The filled box is the cause.
The section's number, then the sheet's place in it.
create_stats.book.mark.idle.means: Wired and waiting: nothing wrong, nothing moving.
create_stats.book.mark.caution.means: Working, but something needs a look.
create_stats.book.mark.fault.means: Will not work until something is fixed.
create_stats.book.one_idea.title: The one idea
create_stats.book.one_idea.hook: A machine has a number. Measure it, move it, show it, act on it.
create_stats.book.one_idea.chain: Measured on the line, carried by a Display Link, shown on a Stats Display; an annunciator sounds when a reading crosses one of its rules.
create_stats.book.one_idea.measure: Takes a reading off a machine or a line: the Power Meter on FE, the Flow Meter on a pipe.
create_stats.book.one_idea.move: Carries the reading. Create's Display Link does it: click the display first, then place the link on the source.
create_stats.book.one_idea.show: Puts it where you can read it: a Stats Display, a Data Dial, a Mini Display.
create_stats.book.one_idea.act: Does something about it: an annunciator sounds, a comparator's signal switches a circuit.
create_stats.book.one_idea.note: When a display shows nothing, walk the chain from the left: does the machine give that number, is the link on that machine, is the display set to show it?
create_stats.book.first_reading.title: Your first reading
create_stats.book.first_reading.hook: A Power Meter on a working line, from placing it to reading it.
create_stats.book.first_reading.step.pla: Hold the meter and click the side of the machine you want to feed. The gland turns to face that machine.
create_stats.book.first_reading.step.sup: Bring power to the brass terminal, which now faces you: a cable from your supply, a connector, or another mod's conduit.
create_stats.book.first_reading.step.ope: Right-click the meter. Its screen opens.
create_stats.book.first_reading.step.rea: Read the word in the window. %s means power is crossing, and the large figure is the FE crossing each tick.
create_stats.book.first_reading.step.els: Any other word: its row on the meter's sheet says why, and the troubleshooting index at the back finds it by name.
create_stats.book.first_reading.note: Nothing to feed yet? Place the meter anyway and wire it later: its word says what is missing.

create_stats.book.way.turn: Arrows, Page Up, Page Down, wheel

create_stats.book.way.pins.does: Point at one and its partners light. Click to turn to them.
create_stats.book.way.ponder.does: Opens a block's scenes. Esc brings you back to this page.

create_stats.book.glossary.title: Glossary
create_stats.book.glossary.hook: The words this book uses, as it uses them.
create_stats.book.term.fe.means: Forge Energy: the power NeoForge mods pass between their blocks. Everything in the Power section carries or uses it.
create_stats.book.term.fe_per_tick.means: FE a tick: how fast power moves. The Power Meter's rate is in it.
create_stats.book.term.tick.means: One step of the game: %s a second.
create_stats.book.term.rate.means: What crosses each tick. The Power Meter shows it as a rolling mean.
create_stats.book.term.peak.means: The most a single tick has carried since the last reset.
create_stats.book.term.supply.means: What gives power: a generator, or storage letting it out.
create_stats.book.term.load.means: What takes power: a machine using it, or storage filling up.
create_stats.book.term.buffer.means: The FE a block holds inside it, waiting to be used or passed on.
create_stats.book.term.comparator.means: The signal, %s to %s, a comparator reads off the block behind it.
create_stats.book.term.display_link.mean: Create's block that carries a reading to a display. Click the display first, then place the link on the source.
create_stats.book.term.goggles.means: Create's Engineer's Goggles. Worn, they show a block's figures as you look at it.
create_stats.book.term.ponder.means: Create's scenes of a block running. Hold the Ponder key over an item, or press a Ponder button on a section's contents.
create_stats.book.term.wrench.means: Create's Wrench. Right-click turns a block in place; sneak right-click picks it up.

create_stats.book.dynamos.title: Dynamos, three grades
create_stats.book.dynamos.hook: Rotation in at the bottom, power out of every other face.
create_stats.book.dynamos.caption: The Kinetic Dynamo on its shaft.
create_stats.book.dynamos.caution: A dynamo is a heavy load on its shaft: at top speed, the stress in its row. A network without that much to spare is overstressed, and every machine on it stops.
create_stats.book.dynamos.application: Set it on a vertical shaft. Run cable from any other face, or set a machine against it and the dynamo feeds it with no wiring.
create_stats.book.dynamos.function.shaft: A vertical shaft under it turns it, either way round. No other face takes a shaft.
create_stats.book.dynamos.function.fan: Turns with the shaft, so a still fan is a still shaft. Sparks fly off the top as it runs, more the faster, and smoke when it is run hard. On the Open Frame the armature itself turns.
create_stats.book.dynamos.function.termi: Where the windings come out. Nothing special to wire: power leaves every face but the bottom.
create_stats.book.dynamos.function.casin: Power out. Run cable to any side or the top, bolt a Power Connector on, or set a machine against it.
create_stats.book.dynamos.gesture.goggle: Output, the buffer, and Create's stress impact at the speed it turns.
create_stats.book.dynamos.status.output: Making power: the shaft's speed times its grade's rate, up to the room in its buffer.
create_stats.book.dynamos.status.idle: Making nothing: the shaft is still, or the buffer is full and nothing draws.
create_stats.book.dynamos.status.capable: The shaft could make more than is taken. The buffer is full; nothing draws the rest.
create_stats.book.dynamos.fault.no_rotat: The shaft is stopped, overstressed, or not under it.
create_stats.book.dynamos.fault.nothing_: Its buffer is full. Wire a load to it.
create_stats.book.dynamos.portrait.capti: Left to right, as in the grades table.
create_stats.book.biofuel_burner.hook: What you feed it sets how long it burns, never how hard.
create_stats.book.biofuel_burner.caption: Front, burning; back, cold.
create_stats.book.biofuel_burner.applica: A hopper above keeps it fed. Power leaves the back and the two flanks, never the door or the mouth.
create_stats.book.biofuel_burner.note: A plant from another mod burns too, if a composter takes it. Coal and blaze rods do not, whatever a furnace makes of them.
create_stats.book.biofuel_burner.functio: Its window glows while a fuel item burns. Nothing is wired to the front.
Takes plant matter, one stack of one kind: by hand, or from a hopper, funnel or chute.
A hanging wire lands on the burner as on a Power Connector. The back gives power too.
create_stats.book.biofuel_burner.gesture: Takes back the fuel waiting in the mouth. The item already burning is spent.
Fills the mouth from any side and marks it fed, so a forecast counts on it burning on.
Reads how full the mouth is.
Drops the fuel in the mouth, and any wires on it.
Making power at its one rate, whatever the fuel.
Time left on the item in the fire, not counting the mouth.
A hopper or funnel keeps it topped up, so a Battery Controller's forecast counts on it.
Nothing draws, so the fire waits for room in the buffer.
Fuel waits in the mouth; it lights once the buffer has room.
The fire is out and the mouth is empty.
Refused: only plant matter burns here.
create_stats.book.biofuel_burner.fault.n: Feed it plant matter by hand, hopper or funnel.
The buffer is full, so the fire waits. Wire the back or a flank to a load.
create_stats.book.solar.title: Solar panels, three grades
create_stats.book.solar.hook: Power follows the sun, and panels joined into a roof earn more each.
create_stats.book.solar.caption: A joined roof, and one panel alone.
create_stats.book.solar.application: One cable against any panel's side or underside collects the whole joined roof. A Capacitor Bank carries the night.
create_stats.book.solar.function.cells: The collector. Give it open sky: glass lets the light through, a block or another panel above does not. Nothing is wired to the top.
create_stats.book.solar.function.rail: Stands round the outside of a joined roof only. Where two panels touch it drops, so one field of cells is one array.
create_stats.book.solar.function.lone: Framed all round: an array of one, with no bonus.
create_stats.book.solar.function.edge: Power out, on every face but the top. Panels touching side by side are one circuit: a cable to one collects them all.
create_stats.book.solar.status.output: What it made last tick: its grade, the sun's height, the sky and the array bonus together.
create_stats.book.solar.status.array: Panels sharing this array's bonus, each counted by the sky it catches, and the bonus.
create_stats.book.solar.status.idle: Making nothing this tick: night, shade, or a full buffer.
create_stats.book.solar.status.night: The sun is down: nothing until sunrise.
create_stats.book.solar.status.holding: Nothing draws, so the panel fills its buffer and holds what it could make.
create_stats.book.solar.status.covered: Another panel above it in its column catches its light.
create_stats.book.solar.status.no_sky: No sky light reaches the cells: something solid is over it.
create_stats.book.solar.status.shaded: Part of the sky is blocked, and the output falls in step.
create_stats.book.solar.status.raining: Rain cuts every panel's output to this share.
create_stats.book.solar.status.thunder: A thunderstorm cuts it further, everywhere at once.
create_stats.book.solar.status.too_littl: Light so faint the panel makes less than one FE a tick, which it rounds to none.
create_stats.book.solar.fault.sun_down.n: Panels work from sunrise to sunset only.
create_stats.book.solar.fault.no_light.n: Clear the column above it: glass is fine, a block or another panel is not.
create_stats.book.solar.fault.nothing_dr: Its buffer is full. Run a cable to any panel's side or underside.
create_stats.book.starter_capacitor.hook: A burst, not a store: when its grid stays short it throws its whole charge at it, then refills from the spare.
create_stats.book.starter_capacitor.capt: Front and back: the apron with the mode box and lamp, and a terminal on each cheek.
create_stats.book.starter_capacitor.valu: %s, only while nothing else is short
create_stats.book.starter_capacitor.appl: A peak shaver: on the machines' own grid it charges from what they leave, and covers them when the grid stays short.
create_stats.book.starter_capacitor.func: Auto fires by itself once the grid has stayed short; Redstone fires on a pulse; Hold charges and never fires. Carried with the block.
Green armed; amber charging, blinking faster through the countdown; red while the arm closes and the burst runs; dark in Hold.
Fill with light as the charge rises, and drain as a burst runs.
The arm swings in before a burst and out after it. What the grid does not take arcs across the gap.
A terminal: a cable or a Power Connector here charges it and takes its burst. The front, back, top and bottom take nothing.
The other terminal, onto the same charge: with a circuit on each cheek it charges from either and fires into both.
create_stats.book.starter_capacitor.gest: Picks it up with its charge and its mode.
Drops it with its charge and its mode, and so does a wrench's sneak right-click.
In Redstone mode a rising edge fires whatever it holds. A world loading with the signal already on is not an edge.
Reads the charge: nothing when empty, full strength when full.
The charge, what it is doing and its mode; sneak for the burst and charge rates.
create_stats.book.goggle.starter_capacit: Ready: fires on a redstone pulse
Burned off in the gap: %s FE
Behind a Power Limiter: a burst cannot reach the panel
On a controller input: fires into it, cannot charge there
Managed: fires when the board or controller comes up short
create_stats.book.starter_capacitor.stat: Full, in Auto: it fires once the grid has stayed short through the countdown. Lamp green.
Full, in Redstone: a pulse fires it. Lamp green.
Taking spare power. Auto will not fire until it is full; Redstone fires whatever it holds. Lamp amber.
Hold mode: it charges and never fires. Lamp dark.
Counting down: its grid has gone short, and it fires when the count runs out unless the grid recovers first. Lamp blinking.
The burst: the arm has closed and its whole charge goes onto the grid, falling to nothing. A grid that recovers does not stop it; Hold or an empty store does. Lamp red.
Every shot empties it: what the grid has not taken this burst arced off in the gap. Here, a grid taking one bank's most a tick.
Nothing on either cheek: it can neither charge nor fire.
Its only circuits are a panel's legs behind a Power Limiter, where a burst would burn off whole, so Auto never fires.
On a Battery Controller input, while a board above that controller is short: the refill that charges it there has stopped until the board recovers.
On a board's or a controller's circuit it fires when that manager leaves something short; a controller refills it before its banks.
create_stats.book.starter_capacitor.faul: Hold charges and never fires: choose Auto or Redstone on the mode box.
Auto fires only when full; Redstone fires whatever it holds.
Grid recovers before the count ends?
Auto needs the shortfall to hold through its whole countdown; a short that flickers never spends a burst.
The words name the wiring that stops a burst: no circuit, a Power Limiter, a controller input.
create_stats.book.starter_capacitor.curv: what it may put out a tick, from full
create_stats.book.starter_capacitor.note: Two on one grid never fire together. The second's count waits while the first fires, and if the grid is still short when the first is done, the second fires at once.
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.hook: Stores FE. Banks that touch join into one bigger battery, worth more than its blocks.
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.caption: One bank, half full, charging on one dynamo.
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.applica: On a plain grid the machines are served first: the bank fills from what they leave and covers exactly what they are short of.
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.functio: A cable, a Power Connector or a machine on any face of any block reaches the whole bank.
The whole bank's charge, lit from the bottom up, the full height of the bank.
The charge, stored over capacity and a bar; under them the flow, CHARGE, DRAW or IDLE, and the time to FULL or EMPTY.
A column a layer of the bank, the lowest filling first: charge goes in at the bottom block and leaves from the top.
Green charging, amber draining, blue holding, red empty.
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.gesture: Moves the whole bank one rank out, and round to the core again; sneak for one rank in. The action bar names it.
Places the next block where the ghost shows and fills out the layer; sneak to place one block alone.
Mined with a pickaxe it drops empty: its charge is lost.
A power readout from any block of the bank.
The whole bank's charge, flow and rank; sneak for how many blocks it pools.
Managed by a Battery Controller: full in ~%s
Managed by a Battery Controller: settles near %s%%
Pooled across %s blocks, fills bottom up
Taking what the machines leave. The figure is the bank's net.
Covering what generation cannot: on a plain grid a bank gives only for a real shortfall, under a controller as its band allows. Empty, the machines go short.
Nothing in or out on balance: full and nothing short, empty and nothing spare, or as much leaving as arriving.
Power passing through, shown only when it charges and drains at once: the line above is the difference.
At its measured net rate. Here, half full on one Kinetic Dynamo's surplus.
At its measured net rate, if nothing changes.
A Battery Controller's forecast, which knows its own policy, in place of the bank's own clock.
The controller foresees the charge coming to rest here: its band never lets ordinary load take the banks to empty.
How many blocks this bank pools. Charge goes into the bottom block first and leaves from the top.
Charged: the whole bank glows evenly, brighter the fuller it is.
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.fault.n: Machines take all the power made?
A grid serves its machines first, and a machine refills its own buffer, before a bank sees any spare. Add generation or take load off.
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.fault.c: It fills its banks from what its outputs leave: its screen's How it decides tab says how much, this tick.
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.fault.w: Part of a wall wider than one bank?
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.fault.o: Your cable is on another bank
Past its largest size a wall splits, a layer at a time, into separate batteries, and only the one a cable touches fills. Wire each, or build stacks one bank wide.
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.fault.n: A bank never fills a bank
Storage is never charged from storage: a full bank and an empty one on one grid stay that way until something generates.
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.joining: Touching banks join, bottom layer first, into banks at most %s wide, %s deep and %s tall. The first block that will not fit starts a new bank, so a wall wider than that splits into separate batteries, each wanting its own cable. A bank in hand shows the next block that still joins.
create_stats.book.capacitor_bank.caution: Breaking a bank loses its charge.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.hoo: Every bank wired to it becomes one reserve with a policy: how hard the banks may be spent, when they refill, and which circuit waits.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.cap: Six terminals on the deck; the face at the moment the screen plates show.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.val: %s, and no more than its wire
create_stats.book.battery_controller.app: Each bank stack on its own input by its own wire, each output one circuit: nothing in series, and the reserve is one number.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.fun: Generators, Capacitor Banks and Starter Capacitors. An input is read from and never served: a machine wired here gets nothing.
One circuit each, numbered as the screen numbers them, served by the plan.
Right-click opens it from any face. With a wire in hand the deck wires instead, and with a cable in hand it does not open.
Takes no cable and feeds no machine set against it: every circuit reaches it through a stud on the deck.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.ges: Click a stud, then the terminal at the far end. The ratings say how many wires a stud holds.
Takes every wire off that stud and gives them back.
Gives back every wire strung to its studs and unhooks the far ends.
A power readout of the reserve.
The reserve's charge, flow, forecast and stance, and any output not fully served; sneak for every output.
create_stats.book.goggle.battery_control: Holding %s FE/t back to refill the banks
Holding %s%% back for a board upstream (the floor is %s%% without it)
No storage wired to any input
%s is wired to a panel leg, which carries nothing
create_stats.book.battery_controller.sta: At or above healthy: ordinary load may draw on the banks freely.
Between the band and healthy: the banks are drawn down toward the band, less freely the lower they go.
Inside the band: ordinary load lives on generation, and what is left of the banks is held. Nothing new comes back on.
Under the floor: the banks give Critical what it asks, less as the last of it runs out, and the highest tiers get it first.
Under healthy, part of generation is taken off what the outputs may spend. It reaches the banks only when the outputs want more than is left; then the lowest tier waits.
A board above expects to go short and has asked for charge to be kept for it: the floor is raised until its supply is back.
No banks: nothing to steer. Wire a Capacitor Bank to an input.
An input wired to a distribution panel's leg stud carries nothing either way. Feed the input from the panel's back boss.
Getting everything it asks for. The goggles print each output's word with what it gets and what it asks.
Short: the bus ran dry before its tier, and it has what was left.
Its breaker is off on the screen.
Held off: the banks are under the floor set on this output. It comes back once they recover past it.
Under its floor with a distribution panel on it: metered to the Critical that panel declares, and the panel sheds the rest.
Set to Surplus, and nothing is spare: it never touches the banks.
Waiting while the refill reaches the banks. It ends by itself as they recover.
Wanted power and got none: higher tiers took it all.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.fau: Open the screen, click the output, and turn its breaker on.
The floor keeps the reserve for the other circuits: lower it, or let the banks recover past it.
Its line on the goggles names the rest: shed by a higher tier, or waiting for the refill.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.now: Now
This tick: what comes in, where it goes, and every setting.
Stance
Where the charge sits against the band, in one word. The reserve's table on the controls sheet says what each means.
Headline
What is happening, in a line, and what it foresees under it; amber or red when something needs a look.
Supply and use
Two bars on one scale: what comes in, generated and from the banks, against where it goes, with anything short hatched on the end.
Inputs
What each input carries, and what it brings in.
Input switch
Isolates an input: the controller stops drawing on it and leaves its circuit to itself until it is switched back on.
The band
Every limit on the banks on one scale: the floor, the band's top and healthy, each with what set it; a board's hold; each output's floor as a numbered pin; the charge as the white marker.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.ban: The same tab with no output open: the band's own panel sits under the columns.
The zones in the stance colours, lit up to the charge and dim past it: the colour under the white marker is the stance.
Drag the floor, the top or the healthy mark along the ruler. In minutes, an edge set where the Critical cannot reach stays put.
Each output's own floor, numbered. Drag one to move that output's floor; it opens the output below.
Minutes of the Critical load, or plain percent of the banks. Switching keeps the band where it is. Defaults, lit when this controller has its own band, goes back to the server's.
The floor, the top and healthy, with what each holds. The blue mark is the charge now.
In minutes, the most of the banks each edge may take, so a small farm still has something above its floor.
What can be dragged and where its controls are.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.now: Outputs
Each output's load, tier, what it gets against what it asks, and why. Click one to open it below.
Breaker
Switches the open output on or off.
Mode
Direct serves all it asks for; Limited never more than its cap; Surplus only what nobody else wants, never from the banks.
Tier
Who is served first when there is not enough for all: the highest tier first.
Floor
Under this charge the output is held off, or metered to its board's Critical. The blue mark is the charge now.
Limit
Limited mode's cap, up to one terminal's rating.
Footer
The open output's own explanation, at the panel's full width.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.for: The controller's own policy, run forward.
The banks' charge over the band's zones: the past left of now, the foreseen to the right. Point at it to read a moment.
Where the past ends and the forecast starts.
Numbered where something happens, the numbers of the list below.
What the inputs bring in, past and foreseen, against the outputs' ask, dotted.
How much of the past the chart shows.
What the forecast takes for granted: the sun, a burner's fuel, the outputs' ask, any hold from a board above.
The supply it assumes, and how far ahead it looks.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.rul: The policy, a step a card, with this tick's figures.
Where the charge sits in the band, and what it lets out of the banks.
The band to scale, the charge marked on it.
How much generation the refill claims: the tick, below, says where it goes.
Each output's tier, mode and floor, what it asked and what it was given, and why.
What the capacitors hold, and what refills them.
What is left over goes into the banks, or what they give instead.
The order the steps run in, every tick.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.tic: Inputs: each input's circuit is taken over, generation sorted from the banks. The banks are the reserve.
Outputs: every load is asked what it wants; a burst fired on an output comes into the bus as generation.
The band: from the charge, what ordinary load and Critical may take from the banks.
The refill: under healthy, part of generation comes off what the outputs may spend, never out of Critical's want.
The plan: breaker, floor, mode, then tier, highest first, out of the bus and the band's allowance, less the refill.
The commit: each output is served out of the bus first, and the banks give only the rest.
Capacitors: Starter Capacitors refill out of what is left, before the banks.
The banks: whatever is still left charges them, the core rank first.
create_stats.book.battery_controller.not: The refill is taken off what the outputs may spend, so it bites only when they want more than generation and the band allow together: then the lowest tier waits and the refill reaches the banks. Otherwise every output is served, out of generation first, and the banks give the rest, refill or not.

create_stats.book.goggle.cord.no_way: No way to lay a cord between those two.
