create_stats.book.goggle.cord.nothing_pl: Nothing is plugged into that socket.
create_stats.book.cables.title: Cable, four grades
create_stats.book.cables.hook: Laid along faces from a source to its loads. A run joins only its own colour, and its grade is what it carries.
create_stats.book.cables.caption: A Kinetic Dynamo feeds two lengths of Bus Duct, which step down to Surface Cable and land on the back of an Induction Smelter.
create_stats.book.cables.application: Lay the heavy grade where the circuit's power runs together, and step down for each branch. Every delivery is charged against each length between the machine and its power, so the thinnest length on its way is its limit.
create_stats.book.cables.function.feed: The run's end in the dynamo, here the source. A run joins any machine it meets on a face that takes power.
create_stats.book.cables.function.joint: On every second length of Bus Duct, dyed with the circuit. Hardware only.
create_stats.book.cables.function.reduce: One grade meeting another: an end fitting each side. They join, and power through it is held to the thinner.
create_stats.book.cables.function.tracer: The stripe in the circuit's colour. Two colours never join, even touching.
create_stats.book.cables.function.elbow: A run turns by itself: flat, into an inside corner, or round an outside edge. A length laid against a run's side makes a tee.
create_stats.book.cables.function.lands: The run's end on the Smelter's back, the one face it takes power on. On any other face a run stops beside it.
create_stats.book.cables.gesture.start.d: Lays a length and starts a run. Click a laid length to carry its run on.
create_stats.book.cables.gesture.again.d: Lays the run there over faces and round corners. On a machine it lands and ends; elsewhere its end stays live.
create_stats.book.cables.gesture.sneak_l: Drops the run in progress. What is laid stays.
Pulls up the whole run of that colour into your inventory.
create_stats.book.cables.gesture.dye: Recolours the whole run for one dye.
create_stats.book.cables.gesture.bore: Takes the run straight through what is in its way, to the same grade beyond.
create_stats.book.cables.gesture.goggles: This length's load against its grade, and why its run carries less.
create_stats.book.cables.status.carrying: This length's own share, not the circuit's: one Kinetic Dynamo at top speed, in the example.
create_stats.book.cables.status.idle: Nothing crossing this length. Idle all along the run: nothing draws, or nothing supplies it.
create_stats.book.cables.status.at_ratin: In red: this length is asked for all its grade carries, and anything more waits.
create_stats.book.cables.status.throttle: A run held below its own grade by thinner cable the circuit's power crosses. The example is the figure's Bus Duct, held by the Surface Cable after it.
create_stats.book.cables.status.held: Past a Power Limiter: the branch takes no more than its setting, here a new limiter's, whatever its cable.
create_stats.book.cables.look.band: A band of light along it
create_stats.book.cables.status.band: Power is crossing. The band runs faster the harder the length works.
create_stats.book.cables.status.amber: At its rating. Lay the next grade up, or split the load.
create_stats.book.cables.status.anchored: The first length is down and the run is live.
create_stats.book.cables.status.laid: The run reached a plain face, so its end stays live for the next click.
create_stats.book.cables.status.connecte: The run reached a machine and ended there.
create_stats.book.cables.status.no_route: No way over faces within the router's reach. Aim nearer, or round the obstacle.
create_stats.book.cables.status.short: The route needs more cable than you hold, and nothing is laid.
create_stats.book.cables.status.ripped: The whole run of that colour is back in your inventory.
create_stats.book.cables.fault.symptom: A machine on the run stays unpowered
create_stats.book.cables.fault.wrong_fac: A run lands only on a face the machine takes power on. Its sheet says which; lay the run to that face.
create_stats.book.cables.fault.two_circu: Two colours never join. Dye the run one colour, or splice the two in a Cable Diagnostic Junction.
create_stats.book.cables.fault.no_supply: Nothing on the circuit makes power, or a breaker or limiter before it is open.
create_stats.book.cables.fault.status_wo: Its goggles name thinner cable or a limiter.
create_stats.book.cables.portrait.captio: Front to back, as in the grades table: Surface Cable, Cable Tray, Bus Duct, Busbar Trunk. Each is dyed its own colour: of one colour, runs laid side by side would join.
create_stats.book.cables.caution: Lengths of one colour side by side join, and a loop is counted down one side, so two runs laid together carry what one carries. For more, lay the next grade up.
create_stats.book.cables.note.config: The grades hold while the server's power.wiring.cableThroughputLimit is on, as it is unless a pack turns it off. Off, each length's rate is its own and sources along a run add up.
create_stats.book.indoor.hook: A slim cord for rooms: clipped to a wall or through the middle of its block, through walls by a bore, and into anything it touches.
create_stats.book.indoor.caption: Bored through a wall, down its face, then across open air into a Water Cooler.
create_stats.book.indoor.application: Drop a spur off a trunk: where Indoor Cable touches surface cable the two join, whatever the grade. The spur's machines share its rating, and the trunk keeps its own.
create_stats.book.indoor.function.gland: Where a bore leaves the wall. Its twin is on the far side, and the run carries on through the wall between them.
create_stats.book.indoor.function.clippe: Held to the wall a pixel and a half off it. An empty hand moves it to the next face or corner, then the middle.
create_stats.book.indoor.function.free: Through the middle of its block. Indoor Cable needs nothing to hold it: it stays where it is put.
create_stats.book.indoor.function.collar: Where the cord enters a machine. A length touching a machine powers it, on any face.
create_stats.book.indoor.gesture.place.d: Clips the length to that face. Click the last length to carry on: the new one takes its clip, and hugs a corner where it meets one.
create_stats.book.indoor.gesture.empty_h: Moves this length to the next face or corner it could clip to, then to the middle.
create_stats.book.indoor.gesture.sneak.d: Gives the whole run this length's clip, as far as each length has a face for it.
create_stats.book.indoor.gesture.dye: Recolours the whole run, through its bores, for one dye.
create_stats.book.indoor.gesture.bore: Click what is in the way, with cable behind you: a straight bore to the same cable on the far side, or to a socket.
create_stats.book.indoor.gesture.pull.do: Pulls the bore that way back out.
create_stats.book.indoor.gesture.goggles: What the run carries, and the bores from this length.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.carrying: The run's share through this length: one Kinetic Dynamo, in the example.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.capacity: What the whole run carries, shared among its machines.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.bores: On a length holding a bore: the run's lengths, and the bores from here. The example is the figure's run.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.clipped: Sneak-click on a clipped length: the whole run took its clip, a plain face or a corner.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.centred: Sneak-click on a free length: the whole run moved to the middle.
create_stats.book.indoor.look.bead: A bead running through a bore
create_stats.book.indoor.status.bead: Power crossing the wall. Both glands show it travelling the same way, from the side that feeds.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.amber: The run at its rating. Below it, the cord pales the harder it works.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.bored: Cut: the far end joins the run. The example is the figure's wall.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.pulled: Pulled: the two ends are apart.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.aim: No cable behind you, or at what you clicked.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.no_partn: No cable of the same kind in a straight line within reach, with something between to bore. Usually the far end is a block out of line.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.nothing: The line holds nothing to bore, or only bedrock or a barrier, which nothing bores.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.already: This length has a bore that way already.
create_stats.book.indoor.status.no_bore: Sneak-click: no bore that way to pull.
create_stats.book.indoor.fault.symptom: A room past the wall stays dark
create_stats.book.indoor.fault.not_bored: Touching a wall is not going through it. Bore it, and a gland shows at each end.
create_stats.book.indoor.fault.bore_drop: A bore with nothing left to pass through is pulled by itself. Join the ends with cable, or rebuild the wall and bore again.
create_stats.book.indoor.fault.no_supply: Nothing feeds the run. Lay it against a trunk, or bore through to one.
create_stats.book.indoor.fault.status_wo: The Cable Bore says why it would not cut, and each length's goggles count its bores.
create_stats.book.indoor.note.spur: A run of Indoor Cable shares one rating among everything it feeds, not one a length. Two spurs off one trunk get one each.
create_stats.book.indoor.note.through: A bore powers every machine it passes through, and a socket at its far end.
create_stats.book.junctions.title: Junction boxes
create_stats.book.junctions.hook: Where runs meet, with a meter behind the door: the cable box splices runs into one circuit, the terminal strip keeps three wired circuits apart.
create_stats.book.junctions.caption: Doors open: the cable box spliced into a run, and the terminal strip with nothing on its studs.
create_stats.book.junctions.application: Splice a spur into a trunk. Every run landing on the cable box is one circuit, whatever its colour, so the box is how two colours are joined on purpose.
create_stats.book.junctions.function.car: Inside the door: the fault codes, so one on the screen is looked up on the spot.
create_stats.book.junctions.function.scr: The cable box: what crosses it against the heaviest cable on it, the load, and the circuit's buffer. The strip: each channel's load and code.
create_stats.book.junctions.function.gla: Top and bottom, where cable runs in. Two runs make a splice; one is a stub.
create_stats.book.junctions.function.lam: Under the screen: the box's state, then on the strip a lamp a channel. Green fine, yellow open or starved, amber a full buffer, red overload or isolated, dark no bus.
create_stats.book.junctions.function.lev: On the strip, behind the door. Up ties all six studs into one bus, down parts them into three channels.
create_stats.book.junctions.function.stu: Three pairs, A on the left to C on the right, each a top stud and the one under it. Wire both and power passes, held to the thinner wire; wire one and the channel is open.
create_stats.book.junctions.function.iso: The handle on the right flank, door shut or open. Pulled, nothing passes the box.
create_stats.book.junctions.gesture.moun: On the side of a block, a girder or a chest. It drops if that goes.
create_stats.book.junctions.gesture.door: Opens or shuts it. Shut, the lamp on its face still shows the box's state.
create_stats.book.junctions.gesture.wire: Strings a span from the stud, as from any terminal. The strip only.
create_stats.book.junctions.gesture.drop: Drops the box, and gives back every wire on its studs.
create_stats.book.junctions.gesture.gogg: The cable box: power, flow and code. The strip: power, mode and each channel. Sneak for more.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.ok: Lamp green. Power crosses the box and nothing is wrong.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.no_bu: Lamp dark. Nothing on it: no cable at a cable box, no wire on a pair.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.open: Lamp yellow. One way in and none out: a single run into a cable box, or one stud of a pair wired.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.starv: Lamp yellow. Wired but dry: the circuit wants more and has nothing left anywhere. Cable box only.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.overl: Lamp red. Carrying all it may, or a cable on it is. Lay the next grade up.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.buffe: Lamp amber. Something on it is full: the machine at a wire's far end, or a connector against a cable box with no cable.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.isola: Lamp red. The isolator is pulled: a choice, not a fault. Nothing passes.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.cut_o: The isolator is pulled, and nothing passes.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.nothi: What the screen says while the isolator is pulled.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.flow: What crosses the cable box against the heaviest cable on it: one Kinetic Dynamo on Surface Cable, in the figure.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.separ: The strip's three channels are three circuits.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.merge: Every stud is on one bus, and power crosses between the pairs.
create_stats.book.junctions.status.lens_: Merged: the studs are one bus.
create_stats.book.junctions.fault.isolat: Throw the handle on the right flank back.
create_stats.book.junctions.fault.stub.n: A splice needs a run in and a run out. Lay the second into the other gland.
create_stats.book.junctions.fault.channe: A channel is a top stud and the one under it. Wire the other.
create_stats.book.junctions.fault.code.n: Look it up on the card inside the door, or in this sheet's fault codes.
create_stats.book.junctions.note.capacit: A cable box's capacity is the heaviest cable landing on it. It is a reading, not a limit: the box holds nothing back, the cables do.
create_stats.book.junctions.note.card: The card also lists %s, %s and %s. No box sets them, so none will ever show.
create_stats.book.outlets.title: Outlets and cords
create_stats.book.outlets.hook: The room's end of a circuit: a socket in the wall, and a cord to whatever stands near it.
create_stats.book.outlets.caption: Fed by cable round the wall's end, with a cord to a bread slicer.
create_stats.book.outlets.application: Bore through the wall from the cable behind it and the socket is live. A cord takes the power on to a machine within its reach.
create_stats.book.outlets.function.feed: Cable against the plate feeds it, as a bore from behind the wall does. A socket never feeds back into wiring.
create_stats.book.outlets.function.lamp: Grey no supply, green live, amber at its rating.
create_stats.book.outlets.function.plug: A cord's plug. A single socket takes one cord, a duplex two.
create_stats.book.outlets.function.cord: Laid round whatever is in the way, and laid again if something is built through it.
create_stats.book.outlets.function.relie: Where the lead lands: the machine's nearest face that takes power, with nothing in front of it.
On the side of a block, a girder or a chest, room side out. It drops if that goes.
create_stats.book.outlets.gesture.bore: Click the socket: the sleeve goes through the wall to the cable behind it, and that circuit feeds the plate.
create_stats.book.outlets.gesture.plug.d: Lays a lead from the socket to the machine, and spends the cord. Plug a single socket again and its lead moves, for another cord.
create_stats.book.outlets.gesture.unplug: Unplugs the lead nearest the click.
create_stats.book.outlets.gesture.beside: Draws with no cord, on the face it turns to the socket, if that face takes power.
create_stats.book.outlets.gesture.link.d: Pairs a switch: the switch decides whether the socket may pass power.
create_stats.book.outlets.gesture.goggle: The socket's state, each lead, and what it needs against what it passes.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.green: Live: the socket holds power to pass.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.amber: At its rating: the socket passes all it can, and more waits. Move a load to another socket.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.grey: No supply behind it, or switched off.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.feeding: Passing power to what is plugged in or beside it.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.live: Live with nothing drawing. A socket a panel has shed reads this too.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.no_supp: Nothing feeds it. Bore through to the cable behind, or lay cable to the plate.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.dead_bo: Bored, but the circuit behind the wall has no power.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.gated: Its paired switch is off: it passes nothing and asks for nothing.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.paired: A switch decides whether it may pass power.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.needs: What is on it asks, against what passed. Live and getting nothing: a panel has shed the socket.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.held: The socket is held. Click the machine.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.plugged: The lead is laid. The figure is the socket's whole rating, shared with all on it.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.unplugg: The lead is out. No cord comes back.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.no_plug: No face of that block takes power with room in front of it.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.too_far: Past a cord's reach. Move the machine nearer, or run cable.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.no_way: No route clear of blocks between them.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.both_fu: A duplex with a lead in each socket. Unplug one first.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.itself: The block clicked was the socket.
create_stats.book.outlets.status.gone: The socket held was broken before the machine was clicked.
create_stats.book.outlets.fault.no_suppl: Bore through to the cable behind the wall, and see that circuit has power.
create_stats.book.outlets.fault.switched: Turn the switch on, or unpair it with the card.
create_stats.book.outlets.fault.shed.not: A Power Distribution Unit has shed the socket. Its lamp stays green and its goggles say live; the panel's device list says shed.
create_stats.book.outlets.fault.status_w: The cord says why it would not plug in, and the goggles what the socket needs against what it passes.
create_stats.book.outlets.note.share: Everything on a plate shares its one rating: both sockets of a duplex, and anything standing beside it. A socket never feeds wiring, a junction box or another socket.
create_stats.book.outlets.caution: Every plug-in spends a cord, and none comes back: not on unplugging, not when the machine goes and the lead drops, and not when a new lead takes a single socket's place.
create_stats.book.connectors.title: Connectors, three grades
create_stats.book.connectors.hook: Bolted to the face of a machine, a battery or a generator: the terminal wire is strung between. It hands its block what its wires carry, up to its grade.
create_stats.book.connectors.caption: An Advanced Power Connector bolted to the back of an Induction Smelter, the face it takes power on, with a Shielded Wire strung from it.
create_stats.book.connectors.application: The connector on the dynamo takes its power and the one on the Smelter feeds it; the span between them carries what its grade carries. Each connector passes the sum of the wires and cable meeting it, up to its own grade.
create_stats.book.connectors.function.te: Where every wire on it lands: copper, gold or bronze by grade.
create_stats.book.keys.wire_then_far_end: Wire: here, then the far end
create_stats.book.connectors.function.sh: Ribbed sheds between the base and the cap: dark ceramic on the Power Connector, white porcelain on the Advanced, black composite on the Industrial, so a grade is told from below.
create_stats.book.connectors.function.ba: Bolted to the face it was placed on, standing out from it. On a slab or a wall panel it shifts toward the slab, so it is always bolted to something.
create_stats.book.connectors.function.bl: The one block it is bolted to. It takes power from it or feeds it, whichever that block does: a generator or a battery behind it is a supply, a machine a load.
create_stats.book.connectors.function.sp: A wire to another terminal. Each span adds its grade to what the connectors at its ends can pass.
create_stats.book.connectors.gesture.pla: Stands out from the face clicked and serves the block behind it. On a slab it shifts onto the slab.
create_stats.book.connectors.gesture.wir: Click it, then a second terminal within reach: one span strung, one wire spent. See Wires and HV Line.
create_stats.book.connectors.gesture.hol: Opens the tension ring once held a moment; a tap never does. With no wires on it, it says so.
create_stats.book.connectors.gesture.wre: Looked at holding a Create wrench, the wrench panel shows above the hotbar: scroll sets the tension, sneak and scroll picks the wire.
create_stats.book.connectors.gesture.str: Strips every wire off it. Each drops here as its own grade, and its far end lets go.
create_stats.book.connectors.gesture.bre: Every wire on it drops here as its own grade, and each far end lets go.
create_stats.book.connectors.gesture.gog: What crosses it, what its block takes or gives, what it can carry as wired, and its wires by grade.
create_stats.book.goggle.connector.held: Branch held to %s FE/t by an inline limiter
create_stats.book.goggle.connector.servi: No wires, serving the block it is on
create_stats.book.goggle.connector.nothi: No wires, no cable, and its block takes no power
create_stats.book.goggle.connector.send_: Send only: a New Age network cannot be drawn from
create_stats.book.connectors.status.carr: What crosses it, its block's share included. Shown when it passes on more than its block takes, as a hub or a pole does: one Kinetic Dynamo at top speed, in the example.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.feed: Its block is a load, or a battery charging: what it takes.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.draw: Its block is a supply, or a battery giving: what it gives.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.bloc: Power crosses it, and its own block takes and gives nothing just now.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.idle: Nothing crosses it, and its block takes nothing.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.capa: What it can carry as wired: its grade, or what its wires and cable carry together if that is less. The example is a Power Connector on one Copper Wire.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.at_r: In red: asked for all it can carry as wired. Anything more waits.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.held: A Power Limiter feeding this circuit holds it below the connector's own figure.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.wire: Every wire on it by grade, against the wires its grade holds: the tension ring's hub, in the example.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.on_c: No wires: the cable touching it feeds it, and counts as a wire would.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.serv: No wires: it serves the block it is bolted to and nothing else.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.noth: Nothing to do: no wire, no cable, and the block behind it takes no power.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.brid: Wires that land on another mod's connector. That mod's goggles will not show them; this line is where to check one.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.send: A wire to a Create New Age connector only sends: their network cannot be drawn from. To take their power, bolt their connector to a terminal of ours.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.more: Behind sneak: why the capacity is what it is.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.rate: Its grade, when its wiring carries at least that much.
Its grade, and the less its wires and cable carry, which is what it can pass: the example's connector.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.cabl: What the cable touching it carries, counted with its wires: a length of Surface Cable, in the example.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.take: The block behind it takes no power, so it serves nothing and only passes power on.
create_stats.book.connectors.fault.sympt: A machine behind a connector stays unpowered
create_stats.book.connectors.fault.wrong: It serves only the block it is bolted to, on that face. A machine that takes power on its back alone wants it there.
create_stats.book.connectors.fault.not_w: String a wire to a connector that has power, or lay cable against it.
create_stats.book.connectors.fault.thin_: Add a span, string a higher grade, or fit higher grade connectors at both ends.
create_stats.book.connectors.fault.statu: Its goggles name a limiter, or a New Age wire that only sends.
create_stats.book.connectors.ring.captio: Example readings: the ring over an Industrial Power Connector strung with one wire of every grade, each at a different tension.
create_stats.book.ring.function.hub: Every wire at once. Point here and scroll: all of them move to one level, starting from the one most share. Its second line is that level, or Mixed.
create_stats.book.ring.function.panel: One for each wire, set the way that wire leaves on screen. Point at one to pick its wire: the panel lights, and so does the wire.
create_stats.book.ring.function.swatch: The wire's own strand colour: what tells two panels apart when their wires leave the same way.
create_stats.book.ring.function.level: How hard the wire is pulled. Wheel up tightens; a click steps one tighter and wraps round to the loosest.
create_stats.book.ring.function.span: Its length, terminal to terminal, and how far its middle hangs below its ends at this level.
create_stats.book.ring.function.pips: The four levels, loosest on the left, the one set raised.
create_stats.book.ring.function.spoke: Dots from the hub toward the panel: the way the wire runs from the connector, on screen.
create_stats.book.ring.function.hint: What the ring answers to. Nothing is set until use is let go; Escape, or walking out of reach, sets nothing.
create_stats.book.ring.function.wire: The wire itself, in the world behind the ring: it hangs at the level being set as the wheel turns, the picked one drawn bright, before anything is applied.
create_stats.book.connectors.wrench.capt: Example readings: the same connector seen holding a wrench, its second wire picked. The panel sits above the hotbar.
create_stats.book.wrench.function.aim: On a connector, with a Create wrench in hand: the panel answers for that connector, with no click.
create_stats.book.wrench.function.all: Raised while the wheel moves every wire at once.
create_stats.book.wrench.function.tab: One for each wire, its grade colour and its number in the order it was strung. The picked one is raised, and its wire lights in the world.
create_stats.book.wrench.function.level: The picked wire's colour and level, or the level most of them share. Each notch is sent at once.
create_stats.book.wrench.function.detail: The picked wire's length and hang; with every wire picked, how many wires there are.
create_stats.book.wrench.function.hint: The wheel sets the level; sneak and the wheel picks the wire.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.no_w: Use held on a connector with no wires, or a wrench on one: there is nothing to set.
create_stats.book.connectors.status.mixe: On the hub: its wires hang at different levels.
create_stats.book.connectors.portrait.ca: Left to right, as in the grades table: Power, Advanced and Industrial, strung with the wire each pair is rated for.
create_stats.book.connectors.note.hub: A connector hands its own block no more than its wires and cable carry, up to its grade, always. What passes through it, span to span, is held to its grade, and each span to its own, while the server's power.wiring.cableThroughputLimit is on, as it is unless a pack turns it off.
create_stats.book.connectors.note.touchi: Two connectors set side by side do not join: only a wire joins them. Cable touching a connector does join it, and counts with its wires.
create_stats.book.wires.title: Wires and HV Line
create_stats.book.wires.hook: Strung across open air from terminal to terminal: four grades, each carrying twice the one before, hung as tight as you like.
create_stats.book.wires.caption: A span of each grade between two stone ledges, each on the connectors it fills: Copper Wire at the back, the HV Line in front, at the standard tension.
create_stats.book.wires.step.connectors: Bolt a connector to each end, on the face each block takes power on.
create_stats.book.wires.step.first: Click the first connector with a wire in hand. It answers: %s
create_stats.book.wires.step.second: Click the second, within reach. It answers: %s One wire is spent.
create_stats.book.wires.step.tension: Set how it hangs: hold use on either end with an empty hand, or look at it holding a wrench.
create_stats.book.wires.step.down: To take it down, break either end, or sneak and click a connector with any wire. The wires drop.
create_stats.book.wires.application: A trunk line: one HV Line fills an Industrial Power Connector at each end, and the far one holds wires enough to fan out to the loads beyond it.
create_stats.book.wires.function.copper: Bare copper, the thinnest: two copper strands in the lay.
create_stats.book.wires.function.shielde: A gold braid over the core.
create_stats.book.wires.function.hv: The heaviest: a graphite jacket with a pale steel screen showing through the lay, the one wire not a colour of metal.
create_stats.book.wires.function.end: Where the span lands: the terminal cap, which every wire on a connector meets.
create_stats.book.wires.gesture.first.do: Anchors a span there: a connector, a machine with its own terminal, or a panel's stud. A full one refuses at once.
create_stats.book.wires.gesture.second.d: Strings the span if the second is within reach and has a free slot, and spends one wire.
create_stats.book.wires.gesture.strip: Strips every wire off the terminal clicked; each drops there as its own grade.
create_stats.book.wires.gesture.hold: On a connector: the tension ring.
create_stats.book.wires.gesture.wrench: On a connector, looked at: the wrench panel.
create_stats.book.wires.gesture.breaking: Breaking either end drops the wire there, and the other end lets go.
create_stats.book.wires.status.attached: The first end is anchored. Click the second terminal.
create_stats.book.wires.status.linked: The span is strung and one wire spent.
create_stats.book.wires.status.too_far: The second end is out of the first's reach: every grade reaches the same.
create_stats.book.wires.status.full: That terminal holds all the wires its grade allows.
create_stats.book.wires.status.already_l: One wire per pair of terminals. The first end is let go.
create_stats.book.wires.status.lost_firs: The first end was broken, or became something that takes no wire.
create_stats.book.wires.status.stripped: Every wire off the terminal clicked, dropped as their own grades.
create_stats.book.wires.status.nothing_t: No wire on the terminal clicked.
create_stats.book.wires.fault.reach.note: Measured block to block between the two ends. Set a connector between them as a relay.
create_stats.book.wires.fault.slots.note: Each grade's wire count is in the connector grades table. Strip one, or fit an Industrial Power Connector, which holds the most.
create_stats.book.wires.fault.one_pair.n: Two terminals take one wire between them. For more, string through a third.
create_stats.book.wires.fault.message.no: Each refusal names its rule in the action bar.
create_stats.book.wires.tensions.caption: Four Copper Wires of one length between two pillars, seen square on. Top to bottom: Slack, Standard, Taut and Drum-tight, as the wheel steps through them.
create_stats.book.wires.note.cosmetic: Tension changes how a span hangs and nothing else. A taut wire carries no more than a slack one.
create_stats.book.wires.caution.ends: A span passes no more than the connectors at its ends: one Shielded Wire between two Power Connectors moves what a Power Connector passes. Upgrade both ends together.
create_stats.book.wires.note.config: A span's grade holds what crosses it while the server's power.wiring.cableThroughputLimit is on, as it is unless a pack turns it off. Off, each connector still hands its own block no more than its wires carry.
create_stats.book.continued_on.words: What each one does, and its status words: sheet %s.
create_stats.book.pdu.hook: A board for one wing of a base. Power comes in at its side bosses; every machine strung to a stud on its bus, or run off its back boss, is served by tier, and when supply falls short the least important go dark first.
create_stats.book.pdu.caption: The back of one board and the front of another, its face at the moment the screen plates show.
create_stats.book.pdu.value.legs: %s: %s studs on the bus, and the back boss
create_stats.book.pdu.value.stud: %s, and no more than its best wire
create_stats.book.pdu.value.back: %s, and no more than its cable
create_stats.book.pdu.application: The feed on a side boss, and a wire from a stud to the Power Connector on each machine. Each stud is a leg the screen meters and can switch off: a hungry machine on a stud of its own, lights and small machines sharing one.
create_stats.book.pdu.function.face: The board at a glance: its mode, the buffer with the reserve floor marked on it, and in Active Auto generation against what is asked and what is served; the roll call along the foot. Right-click anywhere on the board opens the screen, unless a cable is in hand or a wire is on the bus.
create_stats.book.pdu.function.lamps: One a tier, Critical on the left: green when the whole tier is served, steel when part of it is, amber and blinking when none of it is, red when nothing comes in, dark when no machine is at that tier.
create_stats.book.pdu.function.studs: Each stud is a leg. A wire from it to a machine's Power Connector puts that machine on the board. A leg carries what the best wire on its stud carries, up to the stud's rating: wires on one stud do not add up as they do on a connector.
create_stats.book.pdu.function.inputs: The feed, on either side or both: cable, or a Power Connector against the boss. Each takes up to its rating on its own budget. Nothing comes out of a side boss.
create_stats.book.pdu.function.back: The last leg, Back output on the screen: one cable out, for a trunk to another wing or a board downstream. It is held to what the board can spare.
create_stats.book.pdu.gesture.wire: Click a stud on the bus, then the Power Connector at the far end: that stud's leg now serves the machine. The ratings say how many wires a stud holds.
create_stats.book.pdu.gesture.strip: Takes every wire off that stud and gives them back.
create_stats.book.pdu.gesture.drops: Gives back every wire strung to its studs and unhooks the far ends.
create_stats.book.pdu.gesture.display_li: Four lines: machines served of all, what they draw of what they ask, supply and the mode, and the wiring's limit while a leg is full.
create_stats.book.pdu.gesture.goggles: The mode and the branch's served and shed; in Active Auto, generation against demand and how long the buffer lasts. Sneak for the buffer and any battery on a leg.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.mode: How the board serves. Off shares the branch evenly, Manual serves tier by tier until the buffer runs out, Active Auto keeps what the supply sustains.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.branch: Machines getting power, and those held off; amber while any is shed. The Loads view says which, and why.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.gen: Active Auto with no Battery Controller above: generation, then what the running machines cost of what all of them would. Yellow while the ask is over generation.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.reserve_low: Reserve low: what is left is held for Critical
create_stats.book.pdu.status.reserve_low: The banks upstream are down to their last: only Critical may spend it, and nothing lower comes back on.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.export_held: Back boss held: the buffer is below the mark, the branch comes first
create_stats.book.pdu.status.export_held: The back boss asked for more than the board can spare: its own branch is served first, and the back boss gets what is left.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.upstream_of: An upstream panel is not feeding this board right now
create_stats.book.pdu.status.upstream_of: This board hangs off another board's leg, and that board is holding it off. Its row on the board above says why.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.locked_off_: Locked off from the panel upstream
create_stats.book.pdu.status.locked_off_: Switched off by hand on the board above. Set its lock back to Auto there.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.stray_contr: %s runs to a Battery Controller input and carries nothing
create_stats.book.pdu.status.stray_contr: A stud wired to a controller's input feeds nothing. Wire the stud to the connector that input already holds.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.stray_stud: %s runs to another panel's stud and carries nothing
create_stats.book.pdu.status.stray_stud: A stud is an output on both boards. Land the leg on the other board's side boss.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.new_age: New Age connector with no Coupler: fit a Universal Power Coupler between them
create_stats.book.pdu.status.new_age: A Create: New Age connector conducts nothing into this board without a Universal Power Coupler between them.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.face_roll: The roll call along the foot; amber while anything is shed.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.face_no_inp: Nothing in the buffer: no feed reaches a side boss. Every lamp with a machine at its tier turns red.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.lamp_green: Every machine at that tier is served.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.lamp_steel: Part of the tier is served.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.lamp_amber: None of the tier is served.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.lamp_dark: No machine on the board is at that tier.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.locked_on: Locked on by you: Active Auto runs it whatever the sums say, its draw counted first. Manual and Off serve it by its tier, though its row still says pinned on.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.locked_off: Switched off by you, in every mode, and not counted as demand. Its lock back to Auto brings it back.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.over_budget: Shed: the supply does not reach this far down the line. More generation, a higher tier, or less on the board.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.over_capaci: Shed: its leg's wire is full. A heavier wire or another stud; more generation would not help.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.breaker_ope: Its leg is switched off on the screen, or tripped after running over its rating.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.below_floor: Shed: the buffer is under the reserve floor, where only Critical runs.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.tier_shed: Manual: the buffer ran out before its tier.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.awaiting_su: It would fit, but nothing is spare to restart it on: the buffer under the spare mark, no bank charging.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.staged: It fits, and waits its turn: one machine restarts at a time.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.awaiting_dw: Holding its state until the anti-flap time is up.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.core_reserv: Shed: the reserve upstream is being kept for Critical.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.supply_fall: Held: it fits, but the feed's sources say their output falls within the minute. Storage helps, or the sun coming back.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.headroom: Held: it fits the budget, but not yet with the restart margin to spare.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.storage_cha: A battery on a leg, taking charge off the branch.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.storage_dis: A battery on a leg, carrying load the buffer could not.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.storage_ful: A battery on a leg, full.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.storage_idl: A battery on a leg, neither filling nor emptying.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.wire_short: A Spark Crown fed less than it costs: its studs carry no more, and it rides its store down.
create_stats.book.pdu.fault.symptom: A machine on the board stays off
create_stats.book.pdu.fault.switched_off: Select it on Loads and set its lock back to Auto.
create_stats.book.pdu.fault.leg_open.not: Close the leg on the Legs view. A trip means the leg ran over its rating: a heavier wire, or fewer machines on that stud.
create_stats.book.pdu.fault.leg_limit.no: A heavier wire on its stud, or a stud of its own.
create_stats.book.pdu.fault.buffer_first: Raise its tier, feed the board more, or switch to Active Auto.
The table of each machine's state says what every other word means, and what to do.
create_stats.book.pdu.auto.locks: Every machine has a tier, Critical to Optional, and a lock. A machine you locked off is set aside and not counted. One you locked on runs first, and what it draws comes off the budget before anything else.
create_stats.book.pdu.auto.order: The rest are lined up by tier, then by their leg's own rank within a tier, then cheapest first.
create_stats.book.pdu.auto.budgets: While supply is spare, the buffer over the spare mark or a bank charging, everything the legs can carry may run. Otherwise a running machine stays on while the total fits generation plus the buffer above the floor spread over the ride-through, and a shed one comes back only within generation alone, less the restart margin.
create_stats.book.pdu.auto.walk: The line is walked to its end. A machine that does not fit is passed over, and a smaller one further down that does still runs: a lamp can stay lit while a big machine above it waits.
create_stats.book.pdu.auto.restart: A shed machine also waits for spare supply, unless it is Critical, and machines restart one at a time.
create_stats.book.pdu.auto.critical: Critical is judged against generation plus the buffer's ride-through. Under the reserve floor only Critical runs, at once.
create_stats.book.pdu.auto.timers: No machine changes state twice within the anti-flap time, except under the floor or when a generator is added or taken away.
create_stats.book.pdu.auto.manual: Manual serves Critical first, then each tier down from the buffer until it runs out; Off shares the branch evenly. A lock off holds in every mode, a lock on only in Active Auto.
create_stats.book.pdu.value.spare: the buffer over %s%%, or a bank charging
create_stats.book.pdu.value.ride: the buffer above the floor, over %s s
create_stats.book.pdu.value.last_tank: kept for Critical under %s%% of the banks
create_stats.book.pdu.note.critical: Above the floor a running Critical machine is judged against generation plus the buffer's ride-through, which the lower tiers draw on too. With no bank behind the board and generation well short, a big Critical machine can be shed while smaller ones below it run, until the buffer reaches the floor and Critical comes back first.
create_stats.book.pdu.plate.caption: Example readings, at the screen's middle size. A larger window shows more.
create_stats.book.pdu.function.views: The views down the rail, in the order their number keys open them; the lit one is open.
create_stats.book.pdu.keys.select: Click; Shift for a run, Ctrl for one more
How the board serves, in its colour: Off shares the branch evenly, Manual serves tier by tier until the buffer runs out, Active Auto keeps what the supply sustains. Each click goes on to the next.
Gives every machine the tier its kind starts at, over any tier set by hand, so it asks first: it reads SURE? for a moment, and the second click does it.
What feeds the board: generation in Active Auto, what flows in otherwise, with the last few seconds traced under it.
What every machine on the branch asks, the board's own running included, and how many of them are served.
Its charge of its capacity, and under the gauge how long the buffer lasts at this drain before it reaches the reserve floor.
The buffer to scale, the reserve floor ticked on it. Under the tick only Critical runs.

Every tier's draw in serve order, Critical on the left, the served part of each bright; what is served of what is asked above it. The rule marks how much is served, not where shedding starts: when Active Auto passes a tier over, bright bands can stand to its right.
What the board is doing, in a line, and what would change it.
Each tier's machines served of all, and what they draw. Click a tier to list it on Loads.
The status line again, along the foot of every view.
create_stats.book.pdu.loads.function.sea: Lists only the machines whose names hold what you type; Enter goes back to the list.
create_stats.book.pdu.loads.function.gro: Lists the machines under their tier, their kind, their state or their leg.
create_stats.book.pdu.loads.function.she: Lists only the machines being held off.
create_stats.book.pdu.loads.function.gro: A group's name, and at its right its machines served of all and what they draw. Click it to select the whole group.
create_stats.book.pdu.loads.function.row: Its state pip, its tier's colour and its name, numbered when there are several. Click to select it and open the inspector.
create_stats.book.pdu.loads.function.tie: Click for the next tier down the line, right-click for the next up; past either end it comes round.
create_stats.book.pdu.loads.function.pip: Filled, served, and blue when locked on; hollow, shed; a bar, off by you; split, holding; a broken bar, its leg off.
create_stats.book.pdu.loads.function.dra: What it draws now, with a bar of it against the biggest draw listed; a tick behind the bar marks what the board costs it at, where that differs.
create_stats.book.pdu.loads.function.ins: The selected machine: where it is, its leg, what it draws and what the board costs it at, and why it is in its state, in the board's own words.
Its tier, a click away. Under it the lock, Auto, on or off, which a taller window shows whole.
create_stats.book.pdu.loads.function.loc: Copies where it is, to paste wherever you need it.
How many are lit and how many dark, and what the lights draw together.
Puts every light on the board at one tier.
With several rows selected the toolbar turns into this: one click sets a tier on every one. Ctrl and A selects the whole list.
Lock off, lock on, or back to Auto, on every selected row. Locking off a Critical machine asks first.
Drops the selection, and the toolbar comes back.
Click a heading to sort by it, again to turn the order round.
Its state, in a word: the table of each machine's state says what each word means.
Open, Auto: the board decides. Shut and blue, locked on. Shut and faint, off by you.
create_stats.book.pdu.wiring.function.pd: Where every leg starts. Below it the branch as wired, cables and connectors folded into the lines; a thick line is Cable Tray or heavier.
create_stats.book.pdu.wiring.function.sw: A switch on a run: a bar while closed, a lifted lever while open.
create_stats.book.pdu.wiring.function.de: Green while it runs. Click one to select it, as on Loads.
create_stats.book.pdu.wiring.function.sh: Amber, its line dashed: the board is holding it off.
create_stats.book.pdu.wiring.function.lo: Blue: running because you pinned it on.
Faint, its line dashed: switched off by you.
create_stats.book.pdu.wiring.function.ca: How many wires and conductors the branch has, the ceiling its legs add up to, and the FE its wires hold in transit.
create_stats.book.pdu.status.face_modes: The mode, in its own colour: Active Auto green, Manual steel, Off dark. In Active Auto the two thin bars under the buffer are generation, and what is served against what is asked.
create_stats.book.pdu.plate.history_capt: Example readings, at the screen's middle size: the board as it stands, held for the whole range. A larger window shows more.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.function.scen: The branch as built, its real blocks at their real places, slowly turning: light blue glass over this board, red glass over every machine nothing reaches. Drag to turn it, scroll to zoom; from then it holds still, until R puts the view back and the turning on.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.function.hint: What the mouse does here. Once you have turned the view it adds that R puts it back.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.function.tall: How many machines the board is shedding, each under red glass in the scene. Red glass covers a machine you switched off, or one on a leg that is off, too; the count leaves those out.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.function.work: Every figure the decision rested on, in the order the board works it out, and under them its verdict, which a larger window has room for. When the card is full the notes go first, and a long line is cut short with dots.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.function.supp: What the board can count on: generation upstream, what is flowing in now, the reserve above its floor, and the ceiling its legs' wires add up to.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.function.budg: How the run budget is made: generation, less the board's own running and anything leaving by the back boss, plus what the reserve can spend as ride-through. At its foot, the Run budget, what running machines may draw.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.function.row: One row a leg: the eight studs, then the back output. Click a row anywhere but its buttons to list only that leg's machines on Loads. A taller window adds a line under each name, what it carries of its rating, and a bar of it.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.function.tab: The leg's own colour: the Loads and Lighting tables mark each machine's leg with it, and so does the inspector.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.function.stat: What the leg is doing, in a word, its colour a second clue. The tables of the views' words, after the last view, say what each means.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.function.rank: Orders the legs against each other within one tier; click for the next. It changes no machine's tier. A leg with another board on it shows a second chip, BOARD, the tier that board has here, a click away too.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.function.brea: Says what a click does, the opposite of what the leg is doing: OPEN switches a live leg off, CLOSE switches it back on, RESET closes one that tripped.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.function.unwi: A stud with nothing strung to it: no breaker, no rank, and nothing wrong.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.function.back: The back boss, the ninth leg: a cable out, for a trunk or a board downstream.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.function.s: The green area: generation in Active Auto, what arrived otherwise. Its figure is the newest sample's, or the one under the pointer while it is over the chart.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.function.d: The amber line: what the board is asked for, its own running and anything leaving by the back boss included, so both lines describe one board.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.function.r: How far back the chart reaches. Each range is kept apart at its own spacing, so a long range is not a short one stretched.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.function.d: Not history: the board's own forecast of its supply over the coming day, against its Critical load, and who holds any shortfall. It forecasts once it has watched half a day.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.function.p: Supply and demand on one scale, the oldest on the left. Hold the pointer over it to read any sample; the word scrubbing shows while you do.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.function.s: The top of the chart: the largest figure the range holds. A new peak grows it smoothly.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.function.r: A red mark under every sample at which machines were shed, taller for more. A brownout that comes and goes shows here as a pattern you can match to a machine.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.function.to: Swaps the picture for the board's chain in words: what feeds it, the board, and what hangs off it. The button then says Show the flow.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.function.so: Where power comes from, each as wide as what it brings: generators, solar, a Battery Controller, a feed nothing can price, generators on the legs. Point at one for what it is.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.function.fr: The branch takes more than the supply brings, and the buffer pays the rest: the gauge in the middle is falling.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.function.bu: Its buffer as a gauge, how full above it, the reserve floor a line across it. A wider amber line marks charge a board upstream asked it to keep.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.function.si: Where power goes, each as wide as what it takes: what each tier is served, then anything leaving by the back boss, banks charging on the legs, the board's own running, and any spare.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.function.ot: The smallest flows of a column, folded into one so every box can be read. A larger window shows them apart.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.function.sh: Asked for, and not sent: the dashed box the river never reaches. The ladder below says why.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.function.la: Generation as the decision saw it. Hatched grey at its start, what is paid first; hatched amber at its end, what a forecast says is about to go; the blue band under it, what the buffer and any banks add to the run budget.
Each tier's demand on the same scale, in the order Active Auto admits, Critical first: served solid, shed hatched and edged in red.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.function.ad: A shed machine must fit under this to come back.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.function.ru: A running machine keeps drawing while it fits under this.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.function.cr: Critical may ride the reserve down to here; drawn only when it reaches past Run. Where the legs' wires add up to less than the scale, a fourth line, Wire, marks their limit.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.working.run: Everything on the branch is running.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.working.wir: The wiring is the limit, not the supply.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.working.ref: The controller is refilling its reserve.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.working.pro: The controller is protecting its reserve.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.working.unw: Nothing is wired to this panel.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.status.runnin: Every machine on the board is served.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.status.supply: Machines are shed because the supply does not reach them: more generation, a higher tier for what matters, or less on the board.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.status.wiring: A leg's wire is full: a heavier wire, or its load split across more studs. More generation would not help.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.status.refill: A Battery Controller above is holding generation back to refill its banks. It ends on its own.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.status.protec: The banks above sit inside the band their controller keeps: more generation, or a lower band on the controller.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.status.not_au: The board is in Manual or Off, which keep no budget: the working lists the branch alone.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.status.unwire: No wire on any stud, and no cable on the back boss.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.status.no_dev: Wires are strung, but no machine is at their far ends.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.status.over_b: The running machines cost more than the run budget: the buffer covers the gap until it reaches its floor.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.status.at_cap: Asked for more than its wire carries: what does not fit is shed, and if it lasts the breaker trips. A heavier wire, or a stud of its own for the hungriest machine.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.status.trippe: Its breaker threw itself after the leg ran over its rating for too long, and everything on it is off. Lighten the leg, then RESET.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.status.open: You opened its breaker: every machine on it is isolated, and none counts as shed.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.status.unwire: No wire on the stud, or no cable on the back boss: not a fault.
create_stats.book.pdu.legs.status.board_: The board on this leg gets its Critical and nothing more: this board has no spare to send on until its buffer fills.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.history.cov: Covered: the supply carries the critical load all day
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.history.no_: No critical load declared, so nothing to bank for
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.history.sho: Short %s FE before the supply is back%s
create_stats.book.pdu.history.status.gat: Nothing recorded for this range yet: the board keeps its history only while it is loaded.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.status.rai: Machines were shed at that moment; the taller the mark, the more.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.status.lea: The board forecasts the day once it has watched half of it; until then this line counts the hours.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.status.cov: At its lowest the supply still carries the Critical load.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.status.no_: No machine on the board is Critical, so there is nothing to bank for.
create_stats.book.pdu.history.status.sho: At its lowest the supply falls under the Critical load: this is what a bank must hold to carry it until the supply is back. The line under it says who holds it.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.inout.quiet: Nothing is flowing through this board.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.inout.legs_: The legs are the limit, not the supply.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.inout.night: Night outlook: %s FE short before supply is back; asking the boards on its legs to hold it.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.inout.holdi: Holding %s FE back for a board upstream.
create_stats.book.goggle.pdu.inout.not_a: Switch to Active Auto to see a budget.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.from: The branch takes more than the supply brings: the buffer pays the rest, and is falling.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.shed: Asked for, and not sent: what the board is shedding.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.verd: The ladder's verdict, what is held back and which line of the arithmetic held it. This one is the example's; a larger window prints it under the ladder.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.legs: The legs' wires, not the supply, stop more from running: a heavier wire, or another stud.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.nigh: The board foresees a night it cannot carry its Critical through, and asks the boards on its legs to hold their share.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.unpr: Power arrives from sources nothing can price: the board plans on the most it has seen arrive.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.sour: The feed's own generators emptying charge they banked earlier, on top of what they make now. It stops when those buffers are empty.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.hold: A board above, short for the night, asked this one to keep that much charge: it sends less on until it holds it.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.boar: The feed comes through a leg of another board.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.spar: Supply the branch does not spend tops the buffer up; once it is full the box says Spare, idle.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.quie: No power is moving through the board.
create_stats.book.pdu.in_out.status.not_: Manual and Off keep no budget: the ladder is Active Auto's alone.
create_stats.book.pdu.fault.runs.symptom: Machines on the board run, then go off
create_stats.book.pdu.fault.runs.drainin: The branch costs more than the supply. Once the buffer reaches its floor, Active Auto keeps only Critical, and Manual's lower tiers go first. More generation, or less on the board.
create_stats.book.pdu.fault.runs.cuts_in: Each mark is a moment machines were shed: match the pattern to a machine that starts then, and give it a lower tier, so it is the one held back.
create_stats.book.pdu.fault.runs.short_n: At its lowest the supply falls under the Critical load: a Capacitor Bank on its feed or a leg, or a Battery Controller ahead of it, carries it through.
create_stats.book.pdu.fault.runs.end.not: The table of each machine's state says why one is off, and the Flow view's working shows the arithmetic.
create_stats.book.pdu.flow.function.dema: What the machines ask, how much of it was admitted and how much shed, and at its foot the Headroom the run budget has left. When they cost more the line reads Over budget by, and the reserve is covering the gap.

create_stats.ponder.vcc_mk4_aerial_first: Flying a zeppelin from the helm
The VCC Mk IV Aerial flies a zeppelin for you, from its helm
Build it onto the craft, facing the bow
It finds every burner, propeller, fin and lamp, and gives each a job
It proposes, you decide: every job can be changed on its console
Sit in a seat beside the Aerial to take the helm
Hot air gathers under the top of the envelope. Once there is enough, the ship lifts
Seated on the ground, it lifts the ship three blocks and holds it there
create_stats.ponder.vcc_mk4_aerial_altit: Hold %s to raise the height held, and %s to lower it
It brakes before it arrives: gas is slow, so it plans that far ahead
Flown by a lever, a balloon sails past the mark
The Aerial parks on the mark
Load it and the burners answer at once: it weighs the ship every tick
create_stats.ponder.vcc_mk4_aerial_teleg: Tap %s to ring the next order ahead, %s to ring astern
Seven orders, from Full Astern through Stop to Full Ahead
Each order is a share of engine power: Half is half what they can push
The engines answer in about a second, like an engine room
Stop does not coast: it brakes the ship to rest and holds it
create_stats.ponder.seismic_scanner_setu: The Seismic Scanner drops a weight, and its thump maps one target in the ground below
On planks or anything built, the lantern flashes red: there is no natural ground
Stand it on natural ground: stone, dirt, sand, gravel, ice and the like
Hold use on it with an empty hand to open the tuner, then pick a target
Scroll for the radius: %s, %s or %s blocks
Twice the radius costs eight times the FE: the trip dogs rise to mark it
Feed FE into the back or either side of its base, up to %s
The winch hoists the weight: how high it hangs is how much FE it holds
At the trip dogs the pawl drops home and the lantern turns green: ready
create_stats.ponder.seismic_scanner_surv: It reads a bowl of ground under the plate, as deep as its radius, never above it
Pull the lever: the weight drops, and its thump runs out through the ground
The recorder's pen marks the thump and every echo
Each vein lights up as its echo gets back: the nearest first, the farthest last
When the last echo is in, everyone within %s blocks at the blow gets the reading
Only the target answers: the coal stays dark on an iron survey
Each vein shows its ore, its size in blocks and the level it lies at
Back in the ground, the veins glow through the rock for you to dig to
create_stats.ponder.seismic_scanner_read: Stand within %s blocks when the weight lands, and the veins light for you
For %s seconds the whole survey stays lit
Then it fades to what is near you, the far veins first
A vein is plain within %s blocks of you, and gone past %s
Walk on, and veins come up as you near them
Rest your eyes on the rig, or on its recorder up close, to light the whole map
After a relog, rest your eyes on its recorder within %s blocks to read its maps back
create_stats.ponder.power_track_laying.t: Power Track is Create's track with a centre conductor rail: lay it like any track
The rail rides on porcelain chairs, clear of every bogie: only a shoe touches it
Click the track with a Track Feeder, then stand the cabinet beside the line
Wire its back like any machine: a cable to the station's banks
The section is live: the lantern says so. The needle rests at zero until a train comes
A section carries up to %s; each shoe on a car takes %s
Hold use on the rate window to pick Supply, Collect or Auto, and scroll the rate
Goggles on the track read the section, and name every gap in the rail
create_stats.ponder.power_track_collecto: Hang a Current Collector under a car, a block above the track, centred or a block aside
Two or three blocks from a bogie the shoe follows curves best; two shoes a car count
On a live section the car's banks charge, %s a shoe; the sparks mean current
Standing or rolling, a shoe on live metal charges the car
At an insulator the rail stops: the shoe drops to its stop, then arcs as it lands beyond
On a collecting section the car gives, down to that feeder's floor
At the floor the car keeps its charge: the sparks stop and the needle rests
create_stats.ponder.power_track_feeder.t: A Track Feeder ties a section of rail to an FE circuit, like a Portable Power Interface
Supply puts the station's power on the rail, and never drains it below the floor
At the floor the feeder holds: the lantern goes dark and the needle rests at zero
Collect takes power off passing trains, leaving each one its floor's charge
Auto supplies above the floor and collects below it: trains carry power where it is short
The needle swings right while a feeder supplies and left while it collects
The lantern shows the rail: green energised, amber collecting, dark when nothing feeds it
create_stats.ponder.power_track_gaps.tex: A Section Insulator ends a section: nothing crosses its gap; each lamp shows its own side
A feeder on the far side lights its lamp for that section alone
A junction keeps the section: the rail stops clear of the points and jumpers carry it on
The gap is as long as the points: a gentle turnout takes longer to clear than a sharp one
At a change of grade the rail stops %s blocks short each side, clear of a pitching bogie
The slope keeps its own rail between the two ramps; a slope too short for one gets none
A shoe in any gap hangs on its stop and charges nothing: the goggles name each gap
Where the line ends, or ordinary track begins, the rail stops in a plain ramp
create_stats.ponder.powertrack.gap.junct: Junction gap: jumpers carry it on
create_stats.ponder.powertrack.gap.grade: Grade change gap: jumpers carry it on
create_stats.ponder.fe_cables.text_1: Click a face to start a run, then click the machine: the route is laid at once
create_stats.ponder.fe_cables.text_2: The cable carries the dynamo's power to the machine
create_stats.ponder.fe_cables.text_3: Surface Cable carries up to %s: one dynamo is less than a tenth of it
create_stats.ponder.fe_cables.text_4: Four grades, each carrying twice the one before
create_stats.ponder.fe_cables.text_5: Most machines set against a run draw from it too
create_stats.ponder.fe_cables.text_6: Engineer's Goggles show what a run carries against its rating
create_stats.ponder.fe_cables.text_7: Dye recolours the whole run: runs of different colours stay apart
create_stats.ponder.fe_cables.text_8: Sneak-click a run to take all of its cable back at once
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu.text_1: Feed the Power Distribution Unit through either side
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu.text_2: Run a wire from a stud on top to each machine: each wire is a leg
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu.text_3: Open it and give each machine a tier, from Critical down to Optional
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu.text_4: It serves Critical first, and each tier below only from what is left
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu.text_5: In Manual it spends its whole buffer first, then cuts the tiers it cannot feed
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu.text_6: Critical keeps running on what still comes in
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu.text_7: Its screen also switches the mode, and has a breaker for every leg
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu_auto.text_1: Active Auto lines every machine up by tier, Critical first, as on its screen
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu_auto.text_2: Short of power, it first rides its buffer and keeps everything running
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu_auto.text_3: At the restore mark it keeps only what supply and a slow draw on the buffer can run
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu_auto.text_4: What does not fit is skipped, and the smaller machines after it keep running
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu_auto.text_5: As the buffer falls, less fits, and the least important go first
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu_auto.text_6: Back past the mark, it restarts them one at a time, most important first
create_stats.ponder.fe_pdu_auto.text_7: On its screen, lock a machine on so it is never shed, or off so it never runs
create_stats.ponder.fe_wires.text_1: Right-click a connector with wire, then another: a span hangs between them
create_stats.ponder.fe_wires.text_2: Power rides the span to the block the far connector is bolted to
create_stats.ponder.fe_wires.text_3: A connector feeds its block what its wires add up to, up to its own rating
create_stats.ponder.fe_wires.text_4: A second span adds its rating: two Copper spans fill a Power Connector
create_stats.ponder.fe_wires.text_5: A third adds nothing: no connector feeds its block more than its own grade
create_stats.ponder.fe_wires.text_6: Each grade doubles the last, and each connector matches one grade of wire
create_stats.ponder.fe_wires.text_7: Two connectors side by side share nothing until a wire joins them
create_stats.ponder.fe_wires.text_8: Tension changes how a span hangs, never what it carries: hold use empty-handed to set it
create_stats.ponder.fe_wires.text_9: Sneak-right-click a connector with wire to strip it: the wires drop back
create_stats.ponder.fe_capacitor_bank.te: Banks placed together merge into one, and a merged bank holds more than its blocks
Machines are served first: only what is left over charges the bank
Stop the generator and the bank covers exactly what the machines draw
A bank never charges another: the full one runs the range, the empty one stays empty
Break a bank and its charge is gone: it drops as an empty block
Banks merge up to %s by %s and %s high: one cable serves them all
create_stats.ponder.fe_battery_controlle: Inputs A, B and C take generators and banks, outputs 1, 2 and 3 each feed a circuit
Give every bank its own input: nothing is in series, and the reserve is one number
Generation is spent on the circuits first, and what is left charges the banks
Output 3 has a 70% floor: below it that circuit stays off, even with generation to spare
Off generation it spends the reserve, freely while the charge is deep
Lower down it lets out less and less, and the range browns out rather than switching off
Under the floor it is Critical: only a trickle comes out, and the Critical lamp stays lit
Back on generation, part of it refills the banks first: output 1 reads Recharging reserve
On its screen, drag an output's floor, cap its rate, or feed it surplus only
create_stats.ponder.fe_board_and_reserve: Each board asks for three things: its Critical, what else it runs, what it would restore
The controller answers each board with a share and a reason, Critical served first
It runs its own policy forward, and its face says when a board will go short
Short of both, it shares Critical first: board 2's range stops, board 1's runs on
Under the floor it answers Critical only, and each board keeps its own Critical running
Wire an output to a connector on a board's side to give that board a reserve
