gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.machine.positio: Moves something to a place, so it runs only while its key is held
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.machine.runner_: Runs rather than moves to a place, so its key switches it on and off
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.moves.nothing_b: nothing: no light is on Headlight
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.moves.nothing_a: nothing yet: give %s a swivel bearing or a machine (Tools page), a jet (Jets page) or a light (Lights page)
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.moves.nothing_l: nothing: no jet points up or down
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.moves.nothing_s: nothing: no jet pushes sideways through the centre
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.no_governor.hin: No RPM Governor in its shaft line, so the console cannot spin it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.no_jets: No propellers or thrusters on this craft. Andesite, wooden and smart propellers, propeller bearings and Create Propulsion thrusters all count.
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.no_lights: No lights on this vehicle. Put Vehicle Lights on it (white for headlights and reversing, red for tail and brake, amber for signals) and they show up here with their job already picked. A Redstone Link set to receive works too: brake and reverse lights, indicators, headlights on a key, a horn, a cannon's fire.
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.no_tools: No swivel bearings or machines on this vehicle. A swivel bearing (tipping bed, crane, articulated joint) or anything an RPM Governor turns that is not a wheel or a jet (a piston, a pulley, a winch, a drill, a cannon mount) shows up here, ready to put on a key.
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.not_on_craft: Not on a craft. Build the console into a physics craft (Physics Assembler) with the wheel mounts it should drive.
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.nothing_found: Nothing to drive was found on this craft: no wheel mounts, propellers, thrusters or swivel bearings.
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.park_brake.hint: While nobody drives, every wheel is braked, so a parked vehicle stays where it was left
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.preset.all.hint: Every axle steers about the middle of the wheelbase; the rear axles counter-steer
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.preset.crab.hin: Every wheel to the same angle: the vehicle slides sideways without turning
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.preset.front.hi: The front axle steers, everything behind is fixed. Cars and most trucks
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.preset.front_re: Front and rear axles steer opposite ways about the middle. The tightest turn
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.preset.none.hin: No wheel steers: steer with the joint (a swivel bearing on Steer between two halves) or with jets. Every wheel still drives
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.preset.rear.hin: The rear axle steers, everything ahead of it is fixed. Forklifts and telehandlers
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.preset.skid.hin: Nothing steers; the two sides run at different speeds, like a tank. Steer with no throttle to turn on the spot
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.preset.twin_fro: The front two axles steer, the rest is fixed. Needs three axles
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.profile.hint: Wheels by driven wheels on this body, the way trucks are named, and how it steers. Click for the steering
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.relearn.hint: Forget the learned gearing and creep the governors again to learn it afresh
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.rescan.hint: Look for parts again now. The console rescans by itself every few seconds
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.reset_auto.hint: Forget every decision made on this console and go back to what auto proposes
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.reset_keys.hint: Every key back to how it shipped: W and S, A and D, Space, Sprint, Z and X, C
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.reverse.hint: Reverse speed as a share of forward
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.role.fixed.hint: Held straight. The turn centre sits in the middle of the fixed axles
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.role.free.hint: No steering command at all: the mount's own redstone applies
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.role.steer.hint: Points along its circle around the turn centre; behind the centre it counter-steers
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.shares_wheels.h: Its governor also drives wheels, so it spins with them whatever its job
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.aux_a_mi: On while Aux A's other key is held, or toggled by it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.aux_a_pl: On while Aux A's first key is held, or toggled by it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.aux_b_mi: On while Aux B's other key is held, or toggled by it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.aux_b_pl: On while Aux B's first key is held, or toggled by it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.aux_c_mi: On while Aux C's other key is held, or toggled by it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.aux_c_pl: On while Aux C's first key is held, or toggled by it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.aux_d_mi: On while Aux D's other key is held, or toggled by it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.aux_d_pl: On while Aux D's first key is held, or toggled by it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.boost.hi: On while the jets boost: an afterburner's glow
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.brake.hi: On while the wheels brake: the brake key, the reverse key braking, or held at rest
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.tail_bra: Dim while driving, bright while the wheels brake: on a Red Vehicle Light, the tail light and the brake light in one
On while someone drives: dashboard lights, exhaust smoke
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.headligh: Dipped beam while someone drives, full beam on the Full beam key (Keys tab). Toggle on: the key switches full beam on and off. Off: full beam only while it is held, to flash
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.menu_hin: Click to choose what lights it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.source.off.hint: The console leaves this receiver alone
On while driving or rolling backwards
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.speed_steer.hin: The lock shrinks as speed rises, so full stick at speed is a lane change rather than a roll-over
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.status.live: Live: your keys drive the vehicle while this is open.
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.status.sit: Sit in a seat within 2 blocks of the console to drive it.
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.steer_speed.hin: Ticks from centre to full lock while a steer key is held. Fewer is twitchier
You chose this layout. Click here to go back to the one the console proposes
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.steering_label_: The console picked this layout from the vehicle: front steer, twin front on four axles or more, the joint on an articulated vehicle. Click any layout to choose your own
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.swivel.input.hi: Which control moves this bearing. Click to choose
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.swivel.invert.h: Move the other way for the same key
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.swivel.joint_hi: Steers the vehicle at its joint. If A turns you right, press Invert
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.swivel.not_read: Not locked, or nothing attached, so a commanded angle moves nothing. Lock it (redstone or its value panel) and assemble it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tab.board.hint: The vehicle from above, and every key it uses
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tab.jets.hint: Every propeller and thruster, and the job it does
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tab.keys.hint: Which key does what. Click a key to change it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tab.lights.hint: Vehicle Lights and Redstone Link receivers on the vehicle, and what lights each
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tab.parts.hint: Governors, jointed bodies, wheels and problems
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tab.tools.hint: Swivel bearings and machines: beds, cranes, joints, forks, winches, drills
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tab.trailers.hi: What this vehicle tows, how each is joined on, and how the console drives it
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tab.wheels.hint: Which axles steer and drive, and how
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.throttle_ramp.h: Ticks from rest to full throttle, so a heavy vehicle does not spin its wheels or rear up. Braking always acts at once
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.throttle_releas: Ticks from full throttle back to rest when you let go, so the vehicle eases off instead of lurching. By default it follows the throttle ramp; step either way to give it a time of its own. Braking always acts at once
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tie.ground: Tied to the ground: it holds the vehicle back
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.tip.coupler: Against a docking connector: what it gets couples and uncouples
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.title: VCC Mk IV Ground
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.toggle.hint: Each press turns it on or off, like headlights. Off: on only while the key is held, like a horn
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.top_speed.hint: Wheel mount speed at full throttle, in RPM at the mount
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailermode.ass: It carries its own weight. Its drive is worked out from the masses and the wheels so it starts, cruises and stops as you do and you feel no trailer; it brakes a shade before you so its link stays tight; its wheels steer so it follows your path, and hold its angle when you reverse; its jets make up what its wheels cannot
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailermode.mir: Your throttle, brake and Boost as they are, and its wheels straight. Fine when it weighs about what you do per wheel; a heavier one drags on every start and shoves on every stop
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailermode.off: Left alone: not driven, steered or braked, not even by the park brake. It rolls free on its own redstone
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.couple: %s couples and uncouples on %s: a toggle that holds when you leave the seat
A Redstone Link receiver against a docking connector powers it, and a powered connector reaches out and docks with the one it meets. Click for the Lights page
%s couples on %s, which has no key yet: bind one on the Keys page
%s sits against a docking connector: give it a source on the Lights page to couple from the seat
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.intro: Assist: a trailer carries its own weight, brakes a shade before you and steers to follow your path. Mirror: your throttle and brake as they are. Off: left alone.
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.load: Load: no wheels, shown and never driven
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.none: Nothing is hitched on. Join a trailer with a swivel bearing, a rope, a pair of springs or docking connectors, and it shows here with its mode.
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.overru: pushing: its brakes are too weak
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.part_h: Part of this vehicle, on a held joint
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.role.l: No wheels, on a rope or springs: a load on a winch, a boat on a line. It is shown and never driven, and nothing past it is scanned
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.role.p: Part of this vehicle rather than a trailer: the other half of an articulated vehicle, a crane deck, a docked module. Its wheels are held straight, driven with the throttle and braked with the rest
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.role.s: Someone sits at this vehicle's own console, so it is theirs to drive: this console leaves it alone
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.role.t: A vehicle with a console of its own that nobody sits at. While you tow it, its console keeps its park brake off and this one drives its wheels, jets and governors in the mode picked here. Its tools and lights stay its own
A body with wheels of its own hitched on. It is driven in the mode picked here; its tools and lights are yours to use
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.separa: A vehicle of its own, being driven: left alone
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.towed: Towed vehicle, %s wheel(s): its own console yields
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.trailers.traile: Trailer, %s wheel(s), no drive of its own
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.travel.hint: Angle at full deflection, either way
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.turn_nose.hint: Turn the console a quarter to the right. Use it when the console was placed across the vehicle
gui.create_stats.vcc_mk4.wheels.other_bo: + %s wheel(s) on other bodies: a trailer's follow its mode on the Trailers page

block.create_stats.oven.tooltip: An electric oven under a hob. Bakes a filled Cake Mold into a cake and hands the tin back.
block.create_stats.oven.tooltip.placemen: Power goes into the back or either flank, never the front (that is the door) and never the top (that is the hob). Tins go in through the top and finished cakes and empty tins drop out of the underside, so a hopper above feeds it and a hopper below collects from it.
block.create_stats.oven.tooltip.shift: The cavity holds temperature. Preheating costs 128 FE/t and about eighteen seconds from cold; holding costs 35 to 45 FE/t depending on the setting, and standby is 4 FE/t with the light another 2. A bake only advances once the cavity is up to temperature, so the second tin is much quicker than the first. The knob trades peak draw against time rather than total energy: 200 C finishes soonest and asks the most of the grid, 160 C is the gentlest thing to put on a small circuit. Leaving the door open loses heat six times as fast. Losing power pauses the bake without spoiling it, and the cavity cools while it waits.
block.create_stats.oven.tooltip.usage: Open the door, put a filled Cake Mold on the rack, shut the door, press start. Start is a latch, so a belt-fed oven is switched on once and left alone, and it stays hot between tins. The knob picks the temperature and the button beside it works the cavity light. A comparator reads how far through the bake it is, and a full fifteen once the cake is waiting to be taken.

create_stats.jei.oven.info:
The last stage of the baking pipeline. A Cake Mold filled with flavoured Cake Batter goes in, a cake block comes out, and the tin comes back with it: nothing between the Millstone and here consumes a mold, so one tin feeds the machine for ever.

The cavity holds temperature rather than switching on and off with the bake. Preheating from cold draws the full 128 FE/t for about eighteen seconds; once it is up to temperature the elements modulate down to between 35 and 45 FE/t, which is exactly what it takes to replace the heat leaking out. That is why the second tin is quicker than the first, and why leaving the oven switched on between batches is worth doing.

The knob picks 160, 180 or 200 C. Total energy per cake is nearly the same at all three; what changes is peak draw against wall-clock time, which is the number that matters on a small circuit or behind a Power Limiter. Leaving the door open loses heat six times as fast, so the door is worth shutting even though nothing ever locks it.

Tins go in through the top and cakes and empty tins come out of the underside, so a hopper above and a hopper below make it a belt machine. Power goes into the back or either flank. A comparator reads the bake's progress, and a full fifteen once there is something to collect. Losing power, being shed by a Power Distribution Unit or being switched off from a Smart Home Panel all pause the bake where it stands; the cavity cools while it waits, so a long outage costs the preheat and never the cake.

create_stats.jei.surface_cable.info: Tier 1 cable. Carries %s per block, half of Copper Wire. Lay it along block faces: a run turns corners and ends on a machine. Crafted by hand from Copper Wire. The grade above it is Cable Tray.

create_stats.jei.busbar_trunk.info: Tier 4 cable, the top of the cable ladder. Carries %s per block, half of an HV Line. create_stats.jei.copper_wire.info: Tier 1 wire. Carries %1$s per span, and one item strings one span of up to %2$s blocks between terminals. Three per Copper Sheet on a Mechanical Saw, or one per ingot at a crafting table: the only conductor you can still make by hand. A Deployer wraps Dried Kelp onto it for Insulated Wire.
create_stats.jei.copper_wire.saw_note: Create: New Age saws the same sheet into its own wire. A Mechanical Saw with no filter alternates between the two recipes, so filter it for Copper Wire.
create_stats.jei.insulated_wire.info: Tier 2 wire. Carries %1$s per span of up to %2$s blocks, and fills a Power Connector exactly. A Deployer wraps Dried Kelp onto Copper Wire; there is no crafting recipe from this tier up. Sequenced assembly turns it into Shielded Wire.
create_stats.jei.shielded_wire.info: Tier 3 wire. Carries %1$s per span of up to %2$s blocks, and fills an Advanced Power Connector exactly. Sequenced assembly on Insulated Wire: a Golden Sheet braided on, pressed, then jacketed with Insulating Resin from a Spout. Every HV Line has one inside it.
create_stats.jei.hv_line.info: Tier 4 wire, the top of the ladder. Carries %1$s per span of up to %2$s blocks, and fills an Industrial Power Connector exactly. Sequenced assembly on a Sturdy Sheet, two passes: Refined Copper Sheet, press, Insulating Resin, Shielded Wire. It needs a working grid to make, because Refined Copper comes out of the Electric Arc Furnace.
create_stats.jei.power_connector.info: Tier 2 connector. Rated %1$s, the same as Insulated Wire, and holds %2$s wires. A connector passes the sum of its wires up to its own rating, so one Insulated Wire fills it and a Copper Wire fills half.
create_stats.jei.advanced_power_connecto: Tier 3 connector. Rated %1$s, the same as Shielded Wire, and holds %2$s wires. One Shielded Wire fills it; two Insulated Wires do the same.
create_stats.jei.industrial_power_connec: Tier 4 connector. Rated %1$s, the same as an HV Line, and holds %2$s wires: one HV Line fills it, or two Shielded Wires. Made in Mechanical Crafters from two Advanced Power Connectors, four Porcelain Insulators, two Refined Copper Sheets, a Sturdy Sheet and an Electron Tube.
create_stats.jei.refined_copper.info: Arc-refined copper, the conductor of tier 4. Three copper ingots and one sand in the Electric Arc Furnace give two, at %1$s each on Tap %2$s; a run whose arc never dropped gives a third. Press it into Refined Copper Sheet.

create_stats.jei.unfired_insulator.info: Bone china greenware: two Clay Balls, Bone Meal and Flint compacted in a Basin give two. Fire it in a Blast Furnace, an Encased Fan blowing through lava, or the Induction Smelter.

create_stats.jei.seismic_scanner.info:
Drops a weight and maps one target in the rock under it: an ore, the voids or the liquids. Hold use on it with an empty hand to tune the target and a radius of %1$s to %2$s blocks, or scroll with a wrench.

It reads a bowl under the plate, never above it: radius %2$s reads %2$s blocks down. The tuner and the goggles give the deepest level it reaches, and the tuner says when the target is densest outside it. Diamond and redstone lie deepest: carry the rig down to them.

Feed FE into the back or sides of the base. The winch hoists the weight to the trip dogs, %3$s FE for the smallest survey and %4$s for the largest, and the lantern turns green. A comparator reads the hoist and reaches %5$s only when it is ready: carry that full signal back to the rig and it fires itself each time.

Pull the lever or send a redstone pulse to drop it. Only players within %6$s blocks when the weight lands see the veins. The whole map holds for %7$s seconds, then each vein shows by how near you are: plain within %8$s blocks, gone past %9$s. Rest your eyes on the recorder, or point at the rig from underground, to bring the map back. Within %6$s blocks the recorder gives back every target's last map, even after a relog, a portal trip or a blow you missed. Each target keeps its own map until it is surveyed again.

create_stats.ponder.spark_crown.text_1: The Spark Crown keeps chunks of its region loaded and running while nobody is there
create_stats.ponder.spark_crown.text_2: Wire an HV Line to each stud on its back: powered, it holds its own chunk first
create_stats.ponder.spark_crown.text_3: Use it to open its region map, then click the chunks it should hold
create_stats.ponder.spark_crown.text_4: Its own chunk costs 1,024 FE/t, and each further chunk 10% more than the last
create_stats.ponder.spark_crown.text_5: One HV Line carries 20 chunks: the second stud is what takes it to all 25
create_stats.ponder.spark_crown.text_6: At 25 chunks it stands in its ULTIMATE form, drawing 100,707 FE/t
create_stats.ponder.spark_crown.text_7: Cut its power and it rides through on its store: 5 seconds of its draw
create_stats.ponder.spark_crown.text_8: Then every chunk goes at once, its own included
create_stats.ponder.spark_crown.text_9: With power back it takes them back one at a time, each with 5 seconds in store
create_stats.ponder.storm_coil.text_1: The Storm Coil arcs to mobs on FE, and in a storm it catches lightning
create_stats.ponder.storm_coil.text_2: Wire its IN stud to your power: IN charges the capacitor its arcs are paid from
create_stats.ponder.storm_coil.text_3: OUT gives only what lightning banked: power from IN never passes through to OUT
create_stats.ponder.storm_coil.text_4: Raise it on its Height setting: each stage reaches farther and fires at more mobs
create_stats.ponder.storm_coil.text_5: In Hostile mode it arcs at hostile mobs only, a volley a second: the pig is spared
create_stats.ponder.storm_coil.text_6: In a thunderstorm, the tallest thing around, it calls lightning down onto itself
create_stats.ponder.storm_coil.text_7: Each strike banks 9,830,400 FE: its storm bank holds ten
create_stats.ponder.storm_coil.text_8: Now OUT gives the banked lightning out, and IN rests while the bank can pay
